title: Tarouba, Trinidad weather forecast: Day-by-Day rain chances for West Indies vs Pakistan 1st Test 2026
description: Get the day-by-day Tarouba, Trinidad weather forecast and hourly rain probability for the West Indies vs Pakistan 1st Test at Brian Lara Cricket Academy.
fullText:
Tarouba, Trinidad weather forecast: Day-by-Day rain chances for West Indies vs Pakistan 1st Test 2026 originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

West Indies host Pakistan in first Test at Tarouba from July 25.

Babar Azam returns as captain after Shan Masood's removal.

Rain forecast likely to disrupt multiple days of play.

Pakistan and West Indies get their two-match Test series underway on Saturday, July 25, 2026, at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad, though the forecast suggests weather could play as big a role as either team's bowlers over the coming days.

The hosts arrive in good spirits following a solid Test win over Sri Lanka at home, a series that also produced a double-century from Amir Jangoo.

On paper, the quality of West Indies' batting line-up isn't too far removed from Pakistan's, and with Jomel Warrican and Roston Chase both available, the hosts should be well equipped to match Pakistan in the spin department, particularly if conditions in Tarouba favour turn.

For Pakistan, the bigger story heading into this series revolves around fresh changes at the top. Shan Masood's 30-month spell as captain has come to an end, with Babar Azam reclaiming the role he was previously stripped of.

Whether this leadership switch translates into any real improvement remains uncertain, especially given that much of Pakistan's core Test squad has stayed largely unchanged throughout this extended rough patch, raising questions about whether familiar personnel will simply produce familiar results.

MORE: Robin Uthappa blames Babar Azam's lack of Virat Kohli-like mental resilience for batting slump amid 'abuse and disrespect'

Day 1 (Saturday, July 25): Expect rain through the day alongside heavy cloud cover and humidity sitting around 83 percent, conditions likely to disrupt the opening day's proceedings.

Day 2 (Sunday, July 26): A marked improvement is on the cards, with clear skies expected for most of the day, temperatures reaching 33°C, and very little threat of rainfall.

Day 3 (Monday, July 27): Scattered thunderstorms return to the forecast, with humidity near 74 percent and easterly winds around 7 mph likely to interrupt play at points during the day.

Day 4 (Tuesday, July 28): Storms might interrupt play again with the mercury topping out around 29°C. Expect the outfield to turn soggy again, and more stoppages look almost inevitable.

Chance of rain: Moderate to High (55%)

Day 5 (Wednesday, July 29): Scattered showers should return on the closing day, with temperatures climbing back up to 32°C. The good news is that rain isn't expected to linger as long as it has on previous days.

MORE: Shoaib Akhtar likens himself to Ronaldo Nazario if he was a footballer

Rain, heavy cloud cover, high humidity (83%)

Scattered thunderstorms, humidity 74%, easterly winds

Heavy thunderstorms, wet conditions expected

Scattered thunderstorms, reduced delay risk

Rain hovering over three out of five days puts this Test at genuine risk of turning into a shortened affair, and that changes the calculus entirely.

Whichever side can shake off the rust fastest after each stoppage and read a pitch that keeps shifting under damp conditions stands to gain the upper hand, regardless of how the two teams actually compare on paper.

A Test squeezed for time tends to favour boldness over grinding it out session by session. That dynamic could end up suiting Pakistan more than West Indies, given how badly Babar Azam's side needs a result to justify this fresh start under his leadership.

Whereas the hosts might have preferred a full five days to fully capitalise on home advantage and depth built through their recent series win.

title: Sean McCann - brother of Madeleine - makes Commonwealths final
description: Sean McCann, the younger brother of Madeleine McCann, reaches the 400m freestyle final at Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
Sean McCann - the younger brother of Madeleine McCann - qualified for Saturday's 400m freestyle final at the Commonwealth Games by coming through his morning heat in Glasgow.

With parents Kate and Gerry in the stands, McCann finished fourth in his heat and crept into the final as the last of the eight qualifiers at his first major championships.

"I am buzzing," the 21-year-old said. "It wasn't really an expectation coming in given how strong the field was but delighted to see I have made it."

McCann, a chemical engineering student at Loughborough University where he trains, grew up in England but qualifies for Scotland through his father.

He was cheered on by the vocal home crowd at the Tollcross Swimming Centre.

"I could hear them the whole way through the race. It just spurred me on to just give it my all down that last 100m.

"I wouldn't say I was nervous but I certainly felt the pressure with so many people watching.

"I wanted to do well not only for myself but for Team Scotland as well."

McCann and his twin sister, who was also in the Glasgow crowd, were two years old when Madeleine, then aged three, went missing during a family holiday in Praia Da Luz, Portugal, in 2007.

It became one of the world's most high-profile missing-person cases and remains an ongoing Metropolitan Police investigation.

The final, which takes place at 19:07 BST, will include Australia's 2023 world champion and fastest qualifier Sam Short, Northern Ireland's 800m Olympic champion Daniel Wiffen and defending champion Elijah Winnington, plus James Guy and Jack McMillan, who are medal hopes for England and Northern Ireland respectively.

McCann, who has been part of the Scottish Swimming programme since his teens, will also compete in the 800m and 1500m freestyle events later in the meet.

He finished third in the 800m freestyle and fourth in the 1500m at the British Championships earlier this year.

McCann previously competed at the 2024 Championships, which doubled as Team GB's Olympic trials.

Speaking after his heat on Saturday, he admitted the Olympics is his ultimate goal.

"The Olympics is always that step even further," he said.

"Being able to represent Scotland is a good stepping stone on the way to that. Hopefully a couple more years work I will be in the mix for the Olympics."

His progression to the senior Commonwealth Games comes after representing Scotland at the 2023 Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago.

There he finished fifth in the 400m freestyle and seventh in the 1,500m freestyle.

He also raced for Great Britain at the 2025 European Open Water Championships in Croatia.

title: Woking sign ex-Gillingham defender Ogie
description: National League club Woking sign former Gillingham defender Shadrach Ogie on a two-year contract.
fullText:
National League club Woking have signed former Gillingham defender Shadrach Ogie on a two-year contract.

The 24-year-old's three-year stay at Gillingham came to an end earlier this summer when his contract expired.

Woking director of football Jody Brown told the club website that former boss Jermain Defoe "played a big part in identifying and attracting the player to the club before his departure" and said former Leyton Orient man Ogie is "a great fit for what we're building at the club".

title: Vozinha, Cape Verde's breakout World Cup star, joins Chile's Colo-Colo
description: The 40-year-old goalkeeper became known around the world for his performance at the World Cup.
fullText:
Weeks after helping Cape Verde reach the Round of 32 at the 2026 World Cup, star goalkeeper Vozinha has found a new club.

On Friday, Chilean side Colo-Colo announced it has signed the 40-year-old, whose actual name is Josimar Dias, to a reported 18-month free agent contract.

“Welcome. We’re waiting for you,” read the team’s message on social media.

𝐁𝐈𝐄𝐍𝐕𝐄𝐍𝐈𝐃𝐎 
𝐖𝐄𝐋𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐄
𝐁𝐄𝐌-𝐕𝐈𝐍𝐃𝐎

Te esperamos en el Estadio Monumental 🏟⚪️⚫️#VamosCacique pic.twitter.com/ymqPvFTYGS

— Colo-Colo (@ColoColo) July 25, 2026

Colo-Colo, which was founded in 1925, has won the Liga de Primera 34 times, the Copa Chile 14 times and the Copa Libertadores once, among numerous honors. They are currently on pace for another league title as they sit 13 points ahead of Club Deportivo Universidad Católica atop the table.

Vozinha made his mark quickly during Cape Verde’s first-ever World Cup. During the team’s opening match draw against eventual-champion Spain, he made seven saves and became the oldest goalkeeper to record a shutout in a tournament debut. That performance made him a worldwide name, which resulted in his Instagram following skyrocketing from roughly 50,000 followers to nearly 14 million.

As of Saturday morning, that total is now at 29.5 million.

In helping the debutants to a third straight group-stage draw and a place in the knockout round, Vozinha recorded his second clean sheet of the tournament with three saves against Saudi Arabia.

That set up a Round of 32 clash with Lionel Messi and reigning champion Argentina., in what was one of the matches of the tournament, Vozinha stopped eight shots, including four on Messi during a 3-2 defeat that ended Cape Verde’s memorable run.

VOZINHA WITH A CRUCIAL SAVE TO DENY MESSI’S FREE KICK! 🇨🇻 pic.twitter.com/QgF6Kdt8wO

— FOX Sports (@FOXSports) July 3, 2026

Vozinha, who has spent the past three seasons with G.D. Chaves of Portugal's second division, wound up making FIFA’s best XI of the World Cup.

title: Oregon among finalists for elite 2028 recruit, sets commitment date
description: One of Oregon's top targets in the 2028 class is coming off the board, as EDGE Darieon Prescott decides between the Ducks, Notre Dame and Texas A&M.
fullText:
The 2028 recruiting cycle is in full swing, and one of the Oregon Ducks' top targets is about to come off the board.

Four-star edge rusher Darieon Prescott announced he will be committing on July 27, with the Ducks being one of three finalists alongside Notre Dame and Texas A&M. Prescott, from Brookington, Illinois, is ranked as the No. 18 overall player and No. 5 edge rusher in the 2028 class, per the Rivals Industry Ranking.

As of now, Prescott is considered to be leaning toward Notre Dame. He did visit Eugene and College Station in early June, where both programs made a big impression. However, a mid-June trip to South Bend has swung momentum in favor of the Irish. Notre Dame is also close to home for Prescott. He went to two games in South Bend last season and attended a spring practice. Clearly, there is a strong connection with the Irish and coach Marcus Freeman.

The Ducks would love to add another feisty pass rusher to an already elite group in Eugene. The 6-foot-4, 255-pound edge rusher racked up 65 tackles, 14 tackles for loss, five sacks, eight pass breakups and 26 pressures last season. He also forced three fumbles. Prescott uses his size and quickness to wreak havoc in the backfield, and the Ducks have had a keen eye for such talents in recent years.

NEWS: Elite 2028 EDGE Darieon Prescott will announce his Commitment July 27th, he tells me for @Rivals

The 6’5 250 EDGE will choose between Notre Dame, Oregon, and Texas A&M

He’s ranked as the No. 18 Recruit in the 2028 Rivals Industry Rankingshttps://t.co/DVhNMenCTu pic.twitter.com/uVf2CxSE1G

— Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) July 24, 2026

With Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti likely out of the picture next year, the Ducks will have new starters on the edge. Nasir Wyatt, Tank Jones and Elijah Rushing will compete to earn those spots, and Prescott would be a great addition to develop into a starter in the class that follows.

Prescott is expected to announce his decision live on ESPN. The Ducks will have a hat on the table, but the odds might be stacked against them right now. Either way, it is still early in the 2028 recruiting process. Expect the Ducks to continue to push hard, regardless of the commitment.

title: Yankees potential trade target: Reid Detmers
description: Should the Yankees be in play on the second-best lefty on the market?
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels are a mess, and are likely best served by opening the floodgates this trade deadline. They leaked on Thursday that they are interested in trading shortstop Zack Neto, but perhaps the single most-likely-to-be-dealt player on the entire market is lefty starter Reid Detmers.

Detmers just turned 27 and is under team control for two seasons after this. He’s always been decent enough, with a pair of two-win seasons and a strong bullpen year in 2025 that was cut short by elbow injury. This year, it’s a bit of a coming out campaign for Detmers, with a 3.27 FIP and 3.32 xERA contributing to a 3.0 fWAR across 120 innings so far in 2026.

If he played for a functioning franchise, he’d probably be approached with an extension — 3.5-4 win seasons from guys in their age-27 seasons are nothing to sneeze at. But this isn’t a functioning franchise, and the returns from dealing away a player like this are probably 

Detmers features one of the best arrays of breaking pitches in the sport, especially his slider, which he’ll often front door against southpaws and run hard away from right handed batters. It’s been a +14 (!!) run pitch for him this year, running a 35 percent whiff rate. His curveball, which has seen usage drop off this year, gets a whiff 38 percent of the time, and you wonder if the right idea is to lean into pitching backwards even more. Neither of his four-seam nor sinking fastball are all that good, and that may be what keeps him outside the inner circle of elite starters. Then again, the Yankees have had success developing all kinds of fastballs making him the kind of pitcher that fits Matt Blake’s pitching lab — play up the breaking balls that are working, and add some shape to a fastball while in a rotation that features some damn good heaters.

The added benefit of trading for Detmers is that you also functionally trade for a reliever at the same time. We’ve batted around all year which guy in the rotation is best suited to shore up a bullpen that desperately needs some reinforcement, and landing Detmers, who would be a better option than both Ryan Weathers and Will Warren, in my opinion lets you transfer one of those two to the relief corps. Even if you don’t want to do that, you give the rotation margin for rest. You may want to give Max Fried or Gerrit Cole the odd day off, or save Cam Schlittler’s arm in a random September start and hope that helps him in the postseason, and an additional very good pitcher gets you that room to breathe.

The downside is cost. Detmers’ skill and team control means he’s going to be pricey, and you almost drool at the potential he could reach in a pitching lab like the Brewers’. The bidding for Detmers will rival any other player on the market, and if the Angels are able to play that well — a significant if — they should be able to kick start a rebuild off the return.

title: LeBron James contemplated retirement after Thunder swept Lakers

He’d been incredible in L.A.’s first-round upset of the Houston Rockets, playing without Luka Dončić for the whole series and with Austin Reaves for just 64 total minutes in six games. title: Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying: Who takes pole?
description: Who will take pole position at the F1 Hungarian Grand Prix?
fullText:
One qualifying session remains ahead of Formula 1’s August shutdown.

Who will take pole position at the Hungaroring?

It was a “Ferrari Friday” at the Hungarian Grand Prix yesterday, as Charles Leclerc topped the timing sheets in FP1, then finished second to teammate Lewis Hamilton during FP2. In the days leading up to the Hungarian Grand Prix many tapped Ferrari as the favorites, including McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, and those early projections may turn out to be true.

However, teams had all Friday night to pour over the data from the first two hours of practice, and have one more hour of work ahead of the qualifying session. Can anyone catch Ferrari at the Hungaroring?

In a few short hours, we will find out together.

Qualifying gets underway at 10:00 a.m. Eastern on Saturday morning, so follow along with us live!

And don’t forget, you can join the conversation at the all-new F1 Feed! We’ll have a qualifying thread there for you as well, so you can chat as the hour ticks down. For help navigating the feed, we have a handy “how to” post for you to review.

Here is the provisional starting grid for the Hungarian Grand Prix, which will be filled in as the hour unfolds.

title: He is the first player to break 60 on the PGA Tour 49 years before Michael Kim’s 59 at 3M Open
description: Michael Kim wrote his name in golf’s history books, becoming the 15th player to break 60 on the PGA Tour. Kim shot a 59 for a course record at the 3M Open, in a round that featured 12 birdies and no bogeys.
fullText:
Michael Kim wrote his name in golf’s history books, becoming the 15th player to break 60 on the PGA Tour.

Kim shot a 59 for a course record at the 3M Open, in a round that featured 12 birdies and no bogeys. It was the round of his life, and Kim now leads the 3M Open going into the weekend.

It’s the first sub-60 round on tour since Jake Knapp at last year’s Cognizant Classic, but until 1977, no one had ever achieved this feat. It took a 12-foot putt on the final hole for Al Geiberger to become the first in the tour’s then-48-year history.

On Friday, June 10, 1977, during the second round of the Danny Thomas Memphis Classic, Geiberger etched his name into sports history as the first golfer to shoot a 59 in an official PGA Tour event.

Incredibly, he did it at Colonial Country Club, a grueling, par-72 monster stretching over 7,200 yards.

Geiberger, at 39 years old, started his second round on the back nine. He opened with a birdie on the 10th hole, then made six birdies on his opening nine to turn in 30. When he made the turn, Geiberger holed out for an eagle on the 500-yard par five.

Geiberger poured in four more birdies over the next seven holes. In total, his round featured 11 birdies, one eagle, six pars, and no bogeys. His total of 13-under-par 59 required just 23 putts.

On his final hole, Geiberger faced an eight-foot putt for history. He made it for a piece of history.

Just months earlier, his father had tragically died in the Tenerife airport disaster. He then produced a performance for the ages. He went on to win the tournament at 15-under-par.

Geiberger stood alone in golf’s 59 Club for 14 years before Chip Beck matched the feat in 1991. Though several players have since shot 59, and Jim Furyk eventually lowered the PGA Tour record to 58 in 2016, Geiberger’s 1977 round remains the benchmark.

It was achieved on a long par-72 course with traditional equipment. That round still stands alone as the greatest in PGA Tour history.

title: Report – Juventus Plot Ambitious Summer Move for Manchester United Stalwart
description: Serie A giants Juventus are reportedly contemplating an audacious summer move for Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes. According to Turkish journalist Ekrem Konur via Calciomercato, the Turin he...
fullText:
Serie A giants Juventus are reportedly contemplating an audacious summer move for Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes. According to Turkish journalist Ekrem Konur via Calciomercato, the Turin heavyweights view the Portugal international as a potential marquee signing.

Juventus have kept a low profile in the early days of the summer transfer window. Apart from Zeki Celik’s arrival on a Bosman deal, Luciano Spalletti’s men have only signed Jeff Ekhator from Genoa to strengthen their frontline in the wake of Dusan Vlahovic’s departure.

However, Spalletti is keen to add at least one top player to his bloated squad in the coming weeks. With Teun Koopmeiners and Douglas Luiz widely expected to leave Juventus this summer, the former Napoli boss is eager to sign an elite midfielder. Needless to say, the Bianconeri struggled with creativity last season.

Aware of the problem, Spalletti had hoped to lure Bernardo Silva to Turin. Yet, after failing to secure Champions League qualification, Juventus failed to win the race for the Portuguese star, who has joined Real Madrid on a free transfer.

Despite falling short in their effort to sign Silva, Juventus remain hopeful of capturing the services of another Portuguese superstar. Fernandes, who spent five years in Italy before moving to Sporting CP in 2017, has landed on Giovanni Carnevali’s shortlist.

His contract with Manchester United runs out next summer. But that’s arguably the only thing that can encourage Juventus. In addition to captaining the Red Devils, Fernandes has been a vital part of the team over the past six years.

Only last season, he set a new Premier League record for assists in one season, underlining his unparalleled influence. He’d be a major signing for Juventus, but this move doesn’t seem likely to happen.

title: USL records second-highest TV viewership in league history after World Cup
description: The World Cup may be over, but soccer continues to draw strong viewership. A USL Championship match following the World Cup recorded the second-highest TV audience in USL history. The Pittsburgh Riverhounds-Louisville City FC match on July 18 averaged 453,000 viewers. That is the second-highest recorded audience in USL history. The 2024 USL Championship Final…
fullText:
The World Cup may be over, but soccer continues to draw strong viewership. A USL Championship match following the World Cup recorded the second-highest TV audience in USL history.

The Pittsburgh Riverhounds-Louisville City FC match on July 18 averaged 453,000 viewers. That is the second-highest recorded audience in USL history. The 2024 USL Championship Final averaged 606,000 viewers on CBS.

Viewership for Pittsburgh-Louisville was only slightly lower than MLS in primetime on Fox the day before. Nashville-Atlanta averaged 587,000 viewers on Fox. However, unlike the USL, MLS airs all of its games on streaming via Apple TV, meaning it’s unclear how many additional viewers watched on the streamer.

The USL, which operates below MLS in the U.S. soccer pyramid, is attempting to compete with the higher-level league. Its newest media rights deal includes over-the-air exposure on CBS and cable broadcasts on ESPN and CBS Sports Network. MLS has an over-the-air deal with Fox, but the network is not scheduled to air another MLS game until the MLS Cup.

In 2028, the USL plans to launch “USL Premier,” which would compete directly with MLS. Unlike MLS, however, USL Premier is scheduled to feature promotion and relegation from the USL Championship.

The USL Championship still has a way to go to compete with MLS fully. The 2025 MLS Cup averaged 994,000 viewers on Fox and Fox Deportes, which is more than any USL matchup on television. Viewership for the MLS Cup again does not include viewership on Apple TV.

But if this latest viewership mark is any indication, there appears to be momentum for the USL following the World Cup. If the USL wants to compete with MLS one day truly, it will need to continue building on this viewership success.

title: Rams' 26 most important players for 2026 – No. 2: DE Myles Garrett
description: Myles Garrett is entering his first season with the Rams, aiming to take the defense to another level in 2026.
fullText:
Just when it seemed like the Los Angeles Rams were done making moves this offseason, they made their biggest one yet. As the calendar flipped to June, the Rams swung for the fences with a blockbuster trade for Myles Garrett.

They bolstered one of their best positions by adding Garrett, though they did lose Jared Verse in the process. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year joins his best team yet, setting his sights on winning his first Super Bowl.

He debuts on our list of the Rams' 26 most important players at No. 2, one spot ahead of Puka Nacua.

On June 1, the Rams sent Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 second-round pick and 2029 third-round pick to the Browns for Garrett. It was the biggest trade of the offseason, coming out of nowhere after the Rams hadn't been linked to Garrett at any point previously.

Garrett, the No. 1 overall pick in 2017, spent the first nine years of his career in Cleveland as a member of the Browns, winning two Defensive Player of the Year awards and making seven Pro Bowls.

17 games (17 starts): 60 tackles, 23 sacks, 33 tackles for a loss, 39 QB hits, 3 forced fumbles

Though the Rams run a 3-4 scheme, which would put Garrett as an outside linebacker, they're not going to stray from what he does best. He's still going to rush the passer every chance he gets, rarely dropping into coverage, if at all. Chris Shula will move him around as needed, whether it's to the inside in obvious passing situations or on the edge in base sets, but his primary job is going to be to hunt the quarterback.

He and Byron Young will be the primary edge rushers, rarely coming off the field unless they need a breather. Garrett is also a great run defender with his combination of size and speed, so he'll be an asset in that phase, too.

Garrett has earned a PFF grade of at least 92 in each of the last five seasons, finishing first or second among all edge rushers in each of those years. And by now, everyone knows he set the all-time sack record with 23 last season.

The Rams have had a quality pass rush for the last few years, but since Aaron Donald retired, they haven't had a dominant force like Garrett. He's a complete game-changer on the edge, not only as a pass rusher, but also as a run defender.

His athleticism and sheer strength will instill fear in every offensive lineman he faces, forcing teams to adjust their game plans just so he doesn't take over. That opens things up for Young, Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske, giving them more one-on-one matchups.

He'll have the same effect that Donald did for L.A., only as an edge rusher instead of a defensive tackle.

title: Ipswich sign Japan forward Maeda from Celtic
description: Ipswich Town sign Japan forward Daizen Maeda from Celtic on a contract until summer 2029.
fullText:
Ipswich Town have signed Japan forward Daizen Maeda from Celtic on a three-year contract.

The 28-year-old, who has joined the Premier League side in a reported £10m deal, was part of his country's squad at the 2026 World Cup and helped them reach the last 32 before they were knocked out by Brazil.

Maeda scored 79 goals in 212 appearances at Celtic, where he won five league titles, three Scottish Cups and two League cups.

"I have always dreamed of playing in the Premier League and I am very happy I can realise that dream with this club," Maeda told Ipswich's website.

"I have loved all of the conversations with the club and they have made me feel very welcome.

"My aim will always be to battle hard, score goals, and provide assists for my team - I will always run and give everything that I have."

Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil, who took over at Portman Road in the summer following the departure of Kieran McKenna, believes Maeda will be "a valuable member" of his squad.

Maeda joins the Tractor Boys following their promotion back into the top flight after they finished second in the Championship under McKenna last season.

"He works extremely hard and has impressive physical attributes, while also proving over a number of years playing in Scotland that he has the ability to score goals and create for his team," said O'Neil.

Ipswich have added Maeda to the arrivals of defender Issa Diop, winger Abdul Fatawu, striker Emersonn and goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen.

In addition, defender Cedric Kipre and forward Chuba Akpom signed on a permanent basis following successful loans last season.

In a social media post to the "Celtic family", Maeda said "the last four and a half years at Celtic have been the most special chapter of my career and my life".

He added: "It has been an incredible honour to wear this badge, to play for this amazing club, and to share so many unforgettable moments with my teammates, the staff, and the best supporters in the world.

"Thank you for standing by me through every high and low."

When Maeda joined Celtic as a relatively unknown J-League attacker in 2022, no one could have imagined the kind of success he would go on to have at the club.

Maeda arrived in the early days of the Ange Postecoglou era, making the switch from Yokohoma F Marinos to Glasgow initially on loan in late December 2022 before completing a permanent switch in the following summer.

His pace and energy has helped Celtic on numerous occasions but the 2025-26 campaign is what he will be most fondly remembered for.

After failing to replace Kyogo Furuhashi up front, Celtic relied on Maeda to play through the middle for almost the entirety of last season.

Having initially struggled for form, he turned things around when it mattered most.

Maeda was on a barren run of just one goal in 18 games and Celtic were second in the table, trailing league leaders Hearts.

What followed was transformational. Maeda scored seven goals in five Premiership matches, two of which were game winners.

He scored the unforgettable second goal in the final-day decider at home to Hearts when, with the score level at 1-1, Maeda fired beyond Alexander Schwolow on 87 minutes to send Celtic Park wild.

In his final game for Celtic, Maeda opened the scoring in a comfortable Scottish Cup final win over Dunfermline Athletic.

While many fans will be sad to see him go, they probably feel it is a deserved move for a player that has contributed so much.

"His relentless energy and vital goals were an essential part of the team over the past four-and-a-half years, and he was a firm favourite with Celtic fans," said a Celtic statement.

"As he heads on to pastures new at Ipswich Town, everyone at Celtic thanks Daizen for his contribution to the club over the past few years and we wish him all the best for the future."

title: WWE SummerSlam 2026 Card—How Many Matches Will The PLE Feature?
description: WWE SummerSlam 2026 confirmed matches, expected additions and number of matches as Roman Reigns faces Seth Rollins.
fullText:
WWE SummerSlam 2026 will be longer than the typical PLE in more ways than one.

For the second consecutive year, SummerSlam will take place across two nights on Aug. 2 and 3, this time taking place in U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. In addition, the two-night extravaganza will have more matches on each night of the “Big Four” event than the standard PLE.

According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select (h/t TJRWrestling), SummerSlam 2026 is expected to have approximately 12 to 13 matches spread across Saturday and Sunday. This will follow a similar pattern to WrestleMania 42 in April as WWE’s flagship PLE featured seven matches on WrestleMania Saturday and six on Sunday.

Hosting six to seven matches will also represent a notable change from most of WWE’s recent PLEs featuring five or fewer matches.

FORBES | By Blake Oestriecher
Released WWE Stars Officially Hit Free Agency—Here’s The Full List

With a dozen matches now set for SummerSlam, most of the show’s two-night match lineup appears to be set.

Here is the updated card for WWE SummerSlam 2026 following the latest edition of SmackDown:

WWE Championship: CM Punk (c) vs. Cody Rhodes

World Heavyweight Championship: Roman Reigns (c) vs. Seth Rollins

Women’s World Championship: Liv Morgan (c) vs. Iyo Sky

Intercontinental Championship: Penta (c) vs. Chad Gable

United States Championship: Trick Williams (c) vs. Baron Corbin

Hell in a Cell Match: Brock Lesnar vs. Oba Femi

No. 1 Contender’s Match (Winner will challenge for the WWE Title: Finn Balor vs. Sami Zayn

Five-Way Ladder Match for the Interim WWE Women’s Championship: Jade Cargill vs. Tiffany Stratton vs. Charlotte Flair vs. Chelsea Green vs. TBD

The Bloodline (Jacob Fatu and the Usos) vs. LA Knight, Royce Keys and Solo Sikoa

The Bella Twins and Paige vs. Fatal Influence (Fallon Henley, Jacy Jayne and Lainey Reid)

Much of the SummerSlam card has changed significantly from what WWE had originally planned.

Lesnar was expected to face Gunther at WWE SummerSlam, but his last-second move to SmackDown caused a number of changes that also have affected Roman Reigns’ WWE title reign. Similarly, WWE Women’s Champion Rhea Ripley injury resulted in a slew of adjustments to the SummerSlam card. That includes scrapping Ripley’s planned title match as well as Stratton’s United States Championship title defense against newcomer Blake Monroe and a blockbuster singles match between Cargill and Flair.

With WWE potentially having space for an additional match at SummerSlam 2026, WrestleVotes Radio notes that Austin Theory and Bron Breakker of The Vision will potentially defend the World Tag Team Championship on the show. Based on recent storylines on Raw, the likeliest challengers would be Otis and Akira Tozawa.

WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select (h/t F4WOnline.com) also shed some light on which SummerSlam 2026 match could air on the first hour of the broadcast, will air on ESPN in addition to ESPN Unlimited.

That would be the highly anticipated Intercontinental Championship match between Chad Gable and Penta. Gable, who recently became the No. 1 contender, is from Minneapolis, where SummerSlam takes place. That makes his placement in a featured match on the SummerSlam card a no-brainer.

With Penta vs. Gable potentially set to highlight the first hour of SummerSlam, WWE should air at least three other matches on ESPN across the televised portions of the PLE on Saturday and Sunday.

fullText:
Manchester City have confirmed Abdukodir Khusanov has signed a new five-year contract, keeping him at the club until 2031.

Khusanov has significantly enhanced his reputation as one of the best young defenders in Europe after joining Man City in January 2025.

The 22-year-old endured a shaky debut for City, as he struggled in his first Premier League match against Chelsea.

Khusanov became a mainstay in the defence during the second half of the season after injuries to Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol, helping his team win the FA Cup and League Cup trophies.

Earlier in the week, City announced Phil Foden’s contract extension, with the new deal keeping the England international at the Etihad Stadium until 2030.

Foden is one of the best talents to come out of the club’s academy. He endured a difficult 2025-26 campaign and missed out on a place in England’s World Cup squad.

title: ‘YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!’ – Skip Bayless Accuses LeBron James of ‘Ring Chasing’ After 76ers Move
description: Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.
fullText:
Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.

As usual, Bayless didn’t hold back after James ended his three-week hold-up in free agency by going to a team loaded with talent.

The 76ers were reportedly not on James’ radar until they acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. Without giving up VJ Edgecombe or Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia now has a stacked core that is as good, if not better, than any NBA team.

After nearly a month of speculation, the 22-time All-Star snubbed the Miami Heat, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Cleveland Cavaliers, the other frontrunners to get his signature.

A few hours after news broke that James is now a 76er, Bayless reacted.

“CONGRATS, LEBRON! YOU MADE THE OBVIOUS RING-CHASING CHOICE! YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!” Bayless tweeted.

On Friday’s “The Skip Bayless Show,” the veteran sports journalist added more context to his message.

“This wasn’t about basketball happiness! … This was about ring chasing. What team gave LeBron James the best chance to win a fifth, maybe even a sixth championship? It was obviously from the start the Philadelphia 76ers,” Bayless said.

According to Bayless, the 41-year-old superstar wouldn’t take his talents to the Golden State Warriors, which the podcaster named the “Olden State,” if James had gone there.

Bayless continued that he didn’t predict the Timberwolves to win the James sweepstakes, as the 21-time All-NBA wouldn’t want to live in Minneapolis.

The Cavaliers offered a storybook ending, but Bayless didn’t see this version of James as the right fit on that roster.

For the former Fox Sports talk show host, the “happiness” driven decision for James would have been to take his talents back to South Beach, where he could compete for a championship and play golf “all year round.”

The allure of returning to a place where he won two championships and where Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo now lead the roster was not enough to sway James.

MORE: ‘Legacy-Wise, It Didn’t Add Up’ – LeBron James’ Former Teammate Questions NBA Legend’s $8 Million 76ers Deal

Bayless said that it was a no-brainer for James to choose Philadelphia after the 76ers pulled off what he called the “steal of the century” by getting Brown.

The analyst also argued that Maxey and VJ Edgecombe provide enviable youth and speed to surround a player entering his 24th NBA season.

Finally, there is Joel Embiid, who, when healthy, Bayless called the closest the NBA has seen to a Shaquille O’Neal.

Bayless’ criticism of James isn’t new or surprising. Over the past few years, he has been taking shots at the Akron, Ohio, native’s championships, claiming they were won by stacking his teams.

James likely knew he would be criticized regardless of which team he chose to play for. Bayless took his shots, but the only thing that matters to the 76ers’ brand-new acquisition is a chance to win championship No. 5.

title: Roster Rankings: Do Dallas Cowboys Boast NFL's Best 'Triplets'?
description: When it comes to offensive firepower, the Cowboys are better than most, but are they at No. 1?
fullText:
FRISCO - When we hear the word "Triplets,'' every Dallas Cowboys follower is able to speak the language.

One word. And we think of Emmitt Smith, Troy Aikman and Michael Irvin.

History has forgotten the origin. ... They weren't "The Triplets'' until after a couple of Super Bowls, and there was no PR power behind it.

In fact, the legendary sportswriter Frank Luksa coined the phrase, rather innocuously at the time.

And for everyone who was involved with or who was a witness to the "Team of the '90's'' Cowboys, there's been a great effort to attempt to assemble a core-group trio to match Dallas'.

A star quarterback, a stud running back, and an elite receiver.

It can be hard to accomplish all of that in the salary cap era; it does seem like the top teams in football often have a top-10-caliber player at two positions before coming up a bit shy of a super-trio ... let alone an Aikman/Emmitt/Irvin triumverate.

So, what about the Cowboys in 2026?

QB Dak Prescott is coming off one of the best years of his career, throwing for 4,552 yards and 30 TDs; Javonte Williams had a career year with 1,201 yards and 11 TDs; and CeeDee Lamb, while having a down year, still produced 1,070 yards and three TDs.

That is a productive trio, no doubt.

Now, if we are ranking all NFL teams' "Triplets,'' where would Dallas land?

CBS Sports has done that exercise, and the publication has the Cowboys' trio of Dak, Javonte and CeeDee at No. 5.

"Prescott led the NFL in completions and had another 30-touchdown year, while his interception rate once again declined,'' CBS Sports writes.

"Williams put together a better-than-expected debut year in Dallas, and Lamb remains one of the best receivers in the NFL. If we'd been allowed to include multiple receivers in these trios, the Cowboys might've ranked even more highly due to the presence of George Pickens."

No. 10 - Philadelphia - Jalen Hurts, RB: Saquon Barkley, WR: DeVonta Smith.

No. 9 - New England - Drake Maye, RB: Rhamondre Stevenson, WR: A.J. Brown.

No. 8 - San Francisco - Brock Purdy, RB: Christian McCaffrey, WR: Mike Evans.

No. 7 - Buffalo - Josh Allen, RB: James Cook, WR: D.J. Moore.

No. 6 - Kansas City - Patrick Mahomes, RB: Kenneth Walker III, WR: Rashee Rice.

No. 5 - Dallas - Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb.

No. 4 - Baltimore - Lamar Jackson, RB: Derrick Henry, WR: Zay Flowers.

No. 3 - Detroit - Jared Goff, RB: Jahmyr Gibbs, WR: Amon-Ra St. Brown.

No. 2 - Los Angeles - Matthew Stafford, RB: Kyren Williams, WR: Puka Nacua.

No. 1 - Cincinnati - Joe Burrow, RB: Chase Brown, WR: Ja'Marr Chase.

We're digging through this list and we have no real argument with it. ... as the Cowboys are obviously among the NFL's elite. (Maybe Dallas' "Triplets'' are superior to Baltimore's?)

This is a subjective barroom debate, of course. Any "anti-Dallas'' thoughts? Well, Lamb had a down year and Williams only has one good season of production. ... but that's pretty nitpicky.

Put it all together and "These Triplets'' mark another reason for Dallas fans to be hopeful about what 2026 can bring, given the offensive firepower coach Brian Schottenheimer has at his disposal.

Oh, and even though the math doesn't add up - there is no such thing as "Four Triplets'' - George Pickens can't be forgotten in the football part of this equation.

In the end? The ranking demonstrates that the Cowboys have all the tools to once again be a dominant force on offense in 2026.

Dak is coming off a Pro Bowl year, Williams has a chip on his shoulder to prove last season wasn't a fluke, and Lamb has Pickens to push him to new heights.

So, do the Cowboys have the fifth-best set of "Triplets" in football? Should they be ranked higher? Or are they the beneficiaries of "America's Team'' hype?

That, friends, is how we start a barroom argument!

title: Kahn and Schweinsteiger warm that it won't be easy for Klopp
description: Jürgen Klopp is the right choice as German national team coach but he faces huge challenges, former internationals Oliver Kahn and Bastian Schweinsteiger have warned. Kahn told broadcasters BR24Sport that he believes "it won't be as easy as many believe it will be.
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp is the right choice as German national team coach but he faces huge challenges, former internationals Oliver Kahn and Bastian Schweinsteiger have warned.

Kahn told broadcasters BR24Sport that he believes "it won't be as easy as many believe it will be. I believe the problems certainly lie deeper."

The former goalkeeper and Bayern Munich CEO said that Klopp faces many key questions in his new role at the German Football Federation (DFB).

"What kind of players do you want to develop for the coming years? What kind of players do you want in the first place? How do do you want to play football?" Kahn said.

Kahn was speaking on the sidelines of the Bastian Schweinsteiger Cup charity golf event, and its initiator Schweinsteiger agreed that former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool coach Klopp has a big task ahead to make Germany a major football power again.

“Expectations are, of course, very high. You have to start building everything from scratch," 2014 World Cup winner Schweinsteiger said.

"It’ll be quite a challenge for him, but he’s an excellent manager. I think Jürgen Klopp is the right manager for the current situation.”

Schweinsteiger expressed hope “that this sense of optimism will last a long time and that we will get closer to the world’s best again.”

Kahn agreed that Klopp is "a very experienced man who can certainly make a difference."

Klopp, 59, was confirmed as coach on Friday in succession of Julian Nagelsmann who resigned earlier in the month in the wake of a third straight German World Cup fiasco, a last 32 exit against Paraguay.

Klopp has signed a contract until 2030 and will start with four Nations League matches against the Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (twice) between September 24 and October 4.

title: Tony Romo's OWI arrest came after he participated in a golf tournament
description: More details are emerging regarding the arrest of former Cowboys quarterback and current CBS analyst Tony Romo on suspicion of Operating While Intoxicated.
fullText:
More details are emerging regarding the arrest of former Cowboys quarterback and current CBS analyst Tony Romo on suspicion of Operating While Intoxicated. Other important details have not.

From Fox 6 News, apparently the first to obtain the arrest detention report, Romo was in Wisconsin for a golf tournament. He had participated in the Wisconsin Amateur Championship in West Bend, which concluded on Thursday. Romo finished tied in a four-way tie for 73rd.

The arrest reportedly happened on I-43 in Milwaukee, some 40 miles away. Romo is a native of Burlington, Wisconsin.

No indication has emerged as to whether Romo submitted to breath testing to confirm his blood-alcohol concentration. The arrest detention report says that he performed poorly in field sobriety testing.

Romo's first court appearance, on September 21, comes six days before he's due to call the Ravens-Cowboys game in Brazil.

The CBS News website has an item regarding the arrest. The CBS Sports website does not.

ESPN, which has had a rough week for other reasons, has a link to the Romo arrest on its front page and on its NFL page. ESPN NFL Insider Adam Schefter pushed the story on his Twitter firehose.

title: Malik Nabers avoids PUP list, helping his chances of playing Week 2 vs. Rams
description: Malik Nabers wasn’t placed on the PUP list by the Giants, which is a good sign for his chances to play against the Rams early in the year.
fullText:
In Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams are set to host the New York Giants. While that game is months away, one of the storylines revolving around the contest is the health of Malik Nabers.

Nabers, the Giants' star wide receiver, suffered a knee injury last season, and it was widely reported that his recovery wasn't occurring at the expected rate. That report put into question the idea that Nabers may have to miss the Rams' contest.

However, it appears that Nabers' health is back on track. His game status remains a mystery but he cleared a massive hurdle as he was not placed on the Giants' physically unable to perform list.

"New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers is not expected to begin training camp on the physically unable to perform list, a source told ESPN," wrote ESPN's Jordan Raanan. "It's a step in the right direction following a serious knee injury last year."

It was reported that Nabers has spent the summer at the Giants' facility, working to get back into playing shape.

"Working his way into practice as camp gets started one way or the another," stated Giants head coach John Harbaugh. "To what degree, we will find out. But there is a lot of optimism around [Nabers and Skattebo]."

The Giants are set to kick off their training camp with veterans reporting on Tuesday. That will be the first indication of whether Nabers will practice immediately. That was the original goal of both Nabers and the franchise following his knee surgery.

That game against the Giants will be the Rams’ home opener after playing in Australia in Week 1, and it will be the showcase for Monday Night Football.

title: Juan Soto injury update: Latest on Mets star after exiting with calf soreness
description: Soto has had an injury-riddled season
fullText:
Juan Soto can't seem to shake the calf issues he's been dealing with this season. The New York Mets star is slated for an MRI today after exiting Friday's 4-2 loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers with left calf soreness, interim manager Andy Green said postgame.

The five-time All-Star left in the sixth inning after two plate appearances as the designated hitter. Jorge Polanco took his spot and proceeded to strike out twice.

Green admitted he's "concerned" about Soto's calf, which has been bothering him since July 16. Soto has played the outfield sparingly since then in an effort to stay healthy, though he missed the Mets' series finale against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday.

“We certainly hoped we were behind it and done talking about this,” Green said of Soto's calf injury, per MLB.com. “I know it’s frustrating for [Soto], frustrating for us.”

It's not the first calf injury for Soto this season. Back in April, the 27-year-old missed over two weeks due to an unrelated right calf strain.

Soto has been excellent when healthy, however, batting .283/.408/.539 with 21 homers across 84 games.

Jorge Polanco will likely start for Soto as the DH while A.J. Ewing, Luis Robert Jr. and Carson Benge play the outfield.

This article originally appeared on For The Win: Juan Soto injury update: Latest on Mets star after exiting with calf soreness

title: NBA best & worst offseason moves now that LeBron is in Philly
description: The best and the worst moves of the offseason.
fullText:
The entire NBA world has been patiently awaiting LeBron James’ decision. Now that he has decided to team up with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia, all of the big names have signed. That means each team’s roster is, for the most part, finalized.

Whether it has been a blockbuster trade or a superstar signing elsewhere, there have been numerous major moves this offseason. Some of those moves propelled teams into championship contention, while others pushed teams further away from it. Regardless, it’s time to look at the best and worst moves of the offseason.

MORE: NBA world reacts to LeBron James’ stunning 76ers decision

LeBron may have lost a step, but he is still one of the best playmakers in the NBA. James averaged 21 points, 6 rebounds and 7 assists this past season and was a top free agent this summer. Philadelphia already looked like one of the top teams in the NBA, and this move was the cherry on top.

In April, Philadelphia was playing in the play-in tournament. Now, it’s the championship favorite.

Minnesota has been searching for a guard and finally got one, and it isn’t just an average one either. Ball now teams up with Anthony Edwards, and the two are poised to become one of the deadliest backcourts in the NBA.

Philadelphia acquiring Jaylen Brown has to be the top move of the offseason.

Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia in a blockbuster deal this offseason. Brown is coming off an MVP-caliber season in which he led Boston to the second seed in the East. The 76ers got younger and improved at the small forward position.

On top of that, Philadelphia was able to keep V.J. Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey in the trade.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Miami acquires Giannis Antetokounmpo

A player of Antetokounmpo’s caliber can’t hurt a team, but Miami did give up its supporting cast and future for the superstar. The Heat now have no significant players outside of Giannis and Bam.

A failed attempt to sign LeBron leaves the Heat in shambles. Miami went from a play-in team to… a play-in team.

LaMelo was the only bright spot on the Hornets for years and played a huge role in the team’s best season in a decade. Yet they still traded him for Naz Reid. They re-signed Coby White to take his place. White provides scoring but is a far worse playmaker than Ball.

The Hornets took a clear step back with this trade.

Ja Morant looked like one of the best players in the league just a couple of seasons ago before the injuries and off-court issues. Memphis finally traded him this offseason for older players, leaving top-three pick Cameron Boozer with a poor supporting cast.

The Grizzlies didn’t get younger, nor did they improve. It feels like they’re setting their rookie up for failure.

title: Juventus’ Loïs Openda set to join Lyon

This departure marks the premature end of Openda’s Italian adventure, with his spell in Serie A proving to be a failure, having scored just two goals in 34 appearances across all competitions during the 2025-26 season.

In France, the striker will return to a league he knows well, having shone for RC Lens in 2022-23 (21 goals and four assists in 42 appearances), and where he hopes to rediscover his form and return to the level he has shown in recent years.

A notable absentee from Rudi Garcia’s squad for the 2026 World Cup, Openda could also use his move to Ligue 1 as an opportunity to re-establish himself in the Belgian national team, for whom he has made 33 appearances (scoring three goals).

title: Ipswich sign Japan forward Maeda from Celtic
description: Ipswich signed Japan forward Daizen Maeda from Scottish champions Celtic in a deal worth a reported £10 million ($13 million) on Saturday.In  four and a half years with Celtic, Maeda won five Scottish titles, three Scottish Cups and two Scottish League Cups.
fullText:
Ipswich signed Japan forward Daizen Maeda from Scottish champions Celtic in a deal worth a reported £10 million ($13 million) on Saturday.

Maeda agreed a three-year contract with the newly-promoted Premier League club.

In  four and a half years with Celtic, Maeda won five Scottish titles, three Scottish Cups and two Scottish League Cups.

The 28-year-old scored 79 goals in 212 appearances for Celtic.

He was a member of the Japan squad that reached the last 32 at the World Cup before losing to Brazil.

"I am very proud to sign for Ipswich Town. I have always dreamed of playing in the Premier League and I am very happy I can realise that dream with this club," he said.

"I have loved all of the conversations with the club and they have made me feel very welcome.

"My aim will always be to battle hard, score goals, and provide assists for my team – I will always run and give everything that I have."

Ipswich, under new manager Gary O'Neil, have also added Issa Diop, Abdul Fatawu, Emersonn and Kayne van Oevelen in the transfer window.

O'Neil, who took over after Kieran McKenna resigned in the close-season, believes Maeda will make a big impact at Portman Road.

"He works extremely hard and has impressive physical attributes, while also proving over a number of years playing in Scotland that he has the ability to score goals and create for his team," O'Neil said.

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: We're ready for the next thing
description: One of Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's talking points this offseason was the need for the team to "run it forward" after winning the Super Bowl and that mindset was on players' minds on Friday.
fullText:
One of Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's talking points this offseason was the need for the team to "run it forward" after winning the Super Bowl and that mindset was on players' minds on Friday.

The Seahawks have reported to training camp and linebacker Ernest Jones said that his message to the team was that "those wins last year won't help you this year" as they fully turned the page to the 2026 season. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba shared the view that the Seahawks have to put the title in the past and said that he thinks the team is embracing the chance to start all over again.

"It feels like a revamp, a new energy in the building, honestly," Smith-Njigba said, via the team's website. "It feels good to put the past behind us and really focus on the future. On right now in front of us, that's attacking training camp, and I can just tell by the vibe of the guys, talking to them in the locker room, we're ready for that. We're ready for the next thing. It's awesome to be here now."

There will still be reminders of what the Seahawks accomplished in the weeks and months to come because they'll start the season by raising a banner before facing the Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl LXII, but they won't get any boost from what happened in that game and any hope of ending in the same place will be dashed if the team rests on its laurels.

title: How are the Nets affected by LeBron James signing with the 76ers?
description: The Brooklyn Nets have the Philadelphia 76ers' first-round pick in 2028, but with LeBron James signing with them, how is the pick affected?
fullText:
The Brooklyn Nets have been making various moves over the course of the 2026 NBA offseason to try to improve the roster following a 2025-26 season in which they finished with a 20-62 record. Brooklyn has been determined to remain patient over the course of this current rebuild, but a recent move may increase the chances of them getting an extra first-round pick in the future.

ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania announced on Friday that future Hall-of-Famer LeBron James will be signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal with the second year being a player option. While the Nets were likely low on James' list of prospective teams due to their current rebuild, the good news about James signing with the 76ers means that fans in the Tri-state area will be able to see him play more often.

More to the point, the Nets have control of Philadelphia's first-round pick in the 2028 NBA Draft, assuming that the pick falls outside of the top-8 selections for that year. Brooklyn originally received the 76ers' first-round pick in 2028 (top-8 protected) as a result of the trade that sent guard James Harden to Philadelphia and brought Ben Simmons to the Nets during the 2021-22 season.

The only way the Nets would not receive the 76ers' first-round pick in 2028 would be if Philadelphia finished with a poor-enough record to reward them with a pick in the top-8. However, the 76ers finished with the seventh-best record in the Eastern Conference (45-37), but they managed to make it to the second round of the NBA playoffs, meaning that adding James and Jaylen Brown into the fold should only make them more competitive.

As it stands as of this writing, the Nets will have two first-round picks in 2027 (own and via the New York Knicks) and in 2028 (own and via the 76ers). While Philadelphia could have went in a different direction with Paul George approaching the end of his career, the 76ers managed to take advantage of the Boston Celtics trying to unload Brown and now, Brooklyn is essentially more assured of getting a second first-round pick in 2028.

So that 76ers pick Nets hold in 2028 (protected 1-8) will not be high. 🤷🏻‍♂️

title: Former NFL offensive lineman Jorday Devey dies at 38
description: Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died.
fullText:
Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died. He was 38.

Via Jeremy Tombs of Fox 13 in Salt Lake City, Devey died by suicide. His parents told Tombs that they believe Devey suffered from CTE.

Undrafted in 2013 out of Memphis, Devey initially signed with the Ravens but was released. He landed on the Patriots' roster in 2013 and 2014, winning a Super Bowl ring to cap his second year in New England.

Devey spent 2015 with the 49ers, 2016 through 2018 with the Chiefs, 2019 with the Raiders, and 2020 with the Bills. He appeared in 44 regular-season games with 21 starts.

We extend our condolences to Devey's family, friends, teammates and coaches.

title: Barcelona defender earns huge praise from opponent after Europa friendly win: ‘Everything he does is perfect’
description: Barcelona’s first pre-season outing may have taken place behind closed doors, but one player ensured his performance would still become a talking point. The Blaugrana secured a convincing 4-1 victo...
fullText:
Barcelona’s first pre-season outing may have taken place behind closed doors, but one player ensured his performance would still become a talking point.

The Blaugrana secured a convincing 4-1 victory over CE Europa, and while the scoreline itself attracted little attention, one of the opposition players could not stop praising a Barcelona defender after the final whistle.

With transfer speculation continuing to surround Barcelona’s defensive options, Gerard Martin delivered another timely reminder of his qualities during the friendly at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper.

The young defender, who ended last season as one of Hansi Flick’s most trusted players in defence, started alongside Andreas Christensen and looked comfortable throughout the contest.

Calm in possession and confident without the ball, Gerard Martin once again showed why he remains a strong candidate for a regular role in the Barcelona defence.

Gerard Martin started alongside Andreas Christensen. (Picture credit: Instagram/@fcbarcelona)

His display also caught the attention of CE Europa defender Marc Angles, who faced him during the match and later shared his thoughts in a conversation with Gerard Romero on Jijantes.

Reflecting on the performance, Angles was quoted by Mundo Deportivo as saying,

“The one who surprised me the most was Gerard Martin. Honestly, he never puts a foot wrong, and everything he does is perfect.”

Gerard Martin’s influence stretched far beyond his defensive work.

Barcelona beat CE Europa 4-1 in pre-season friendly. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona)

One of the biggest moments of the match came when he broke through the opposition’s defensive line with an accurate forward pass that released Ibrahim Diarra, who converted to give Barcelona the opening goal.

It was a moment that showed the defender’s composure and passing range, qualities that have become increasingly valuable in Flick’s tactical approach.

Defensively, Gerard Martin was equally reliable. He remained composed under pressure, won his duels and displayed impressive physical sharpness despite only recently returning from the summer break.

His overall display suggested he has returned to pre-season in excellent condition and ready to compete from the very beginning.

title: Abhishek Sharma vs Blessing Muzarabani in T20Is: India batter's shockingly poor head-to-head record against Zimbabwe pacer
description: While the Indian T20 side has made short work of the Zimbabwean bowling, Abhishek Sharma's batting has been less than optimal, as he was sent back to the pavilion within the second over.
fullText:
Abhishek Sharma vs Blessing Muzarabani in T20Is: India batter's shockingly poor head-to-head record against Zimbabwe pacer originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Abhishek Sharma has scored just 8 runs off Blessing Muzarabani across their T20I meetings.

The Zimbabwe pacer has dismissed the India opener three times in 21 balls.

Muzarabani's extra bounce has repeatedly troubled the left-hander at Harare.

Abhishek Sharma is one of the most destructive openers in world cricket, a batter whose fearless hitting has redefined how India start a T20 innings. Yet there is one bowler who has consistently found a way to shut him down.

That man is Blessing Muzarabani. The towering Zimbabwe seamer has turned his personal battle with Abhishek into one of the most lopsided head-to-head records in the format, and he added another chapter to it in the second T20I in Harare on Thursday.

The 6 ft 8 in (2.03 m) paceman removed Abhishek for the third time in T20Is, extracting the extra bounce that has repeatedly undone the left-hander at this venue and leaving his overall numbers against Muzarabani remarkably poor. In fact, in just this series, Muzarabani has dismissed Sharma in both the first and second T20Is.

MORE: India's 'Best Attitude Award' winners during Zimbabwe T20I series: Full list

Across their two years of meetings, Abhishek has managed just eight runs from 21 balls against Muzarabani while being dismissed three times, an average of 2.7 and a strike rate of 38.1.

The 2026 figures are especially stark. Abhishek has faced 14 balls from Muzarabani this year for just three runs, playing out 11 dots and failing to find the boundary even once against a bowler he would normally look to attack.

Thursday's dismissal followed the familiar script. Muzarabani conceded only three runs in his first two overs before Abhishek, struggling to hit through the line on a two-paced pitch, holed out to Brad Evans at third man.

MORE: 'Crush his confidence': Srikkanth slams Gambhir's treatment of Sooryavanshi

The mismatch is largely about height and bounce. Abhishek's game is built on hitting through the line and swinging across it, which works against bowlers who let the ball come onto the bat, but Muzarabani's steep bounce from a good length denies him exactly that. Harare accentuates the problem.

The surface offers early moisture and spongy bounce, and a bowler of Muzarabani's height extracts more from it than anyone, leaving Abhishek reaching for balls that climb higher than he anticipates. The contrast with his teammate is telling. Where Abhishek was tied down on Thursday, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi took Muzarabani for a ride.

The youngster hit the seamer for two fours and a six in a single over, suggesting the answer lies in adjusting rather than in the bowler being unplayable.

That is the real intrigue heading into the second T20I. Abhishek remains far too good a player to stay quiet for long, but until he solves the bounce, this is a matchup Muzarabani will keep targeting every time the two meet.

title: Kerry v Mayo - triumph, pain and 'the curse'
description: All-Ireland champions Kerry put their title on the line against Mayo, who are eager to end their 75-year wait for Sam Maguire.
fullText:
In the build-up to last year's All-Ireland final, former Kerry captain Dara Ó Cinnéide pointed out "nobody has lost more finals than Kerry".

It's true, as while the Kingdom lead the way on the roll of honour with 39 Sam Maguire triumphs, their 24 defeats on Gaelic football's biggest day is greater than any other county.

Cork are next in that unwanted bracket with 16, but just one behind - level with Galway - sits Mayo.

The Yew County must go back 75 years for the last of their three All-Ireland titles, defending the crown they had won the previous season, but while All-Ireland success has eluded them since, a return to the final was 44 years in the making.

In 1989, led by the late John O'Mahony, Mayo rolled into Croke Park to face a Cork side that had fallen short in the previous two finals against Meath - the second of those after a replay.

Perhaps there was a sense that it was the Rebels' time, but Mayo had their chances, only to fall to a three-point defeat. It would prove to be the first of 11 disappointments on final day.

All-Ireland Senior Football Championship final

Watch live on BBC Two, BBC Sport website & app from 15:00

They were back seven years later, thanks to a semi-final win over Kerry who were ready to challenge again after a number of years in the wilderness, but after Colm Coyle's late punt hopped off the ground and over the bar to force a draw, Meath won a replay that was marred by an early brawl.

Certainly, there was an element of fortune in Meath's equaliser in the drawn game, but could it be something a lot deeper for Mayo? A curse, perhaps?

As the story - or myth - goes, following their 1951 win and on their way home on to Castlebar on an open-back lorry, the team's boisterous celebrations interrupted a funeral taking place in Foxford, just outside Ballina with the presiding priest laying a curse that Mayo would not win an All-Ireland title any member of the team was alive.

Whether that is fact or folklore remains unclear, but Mayo's fortunes on All-Ireland final day have not improved since.

The following year, they returned to the decider against Kerry who would make up for the previous year's semi-final reverse with a three-point win.

It would not be misfortune for Mayo, but the brilliance of Maurice Fitzgerald that was the difference, with the Cahersiveen man kicking nine points on the day.

Those two meetings between the counties would prove to be the beginning of a new-found rivalry.

Kerry would return to the top in 2000, marking the start of a successful decade as Sam Maguire would return to the Kingdom on five occasions, with three further final defeats in this time.

In 2004, Mayo were back in the final to meet them and while Alan Dillon netted an early goal, the game would quickly get away from them as Colm Cooper goaled at the other end on a day in which he and Ó Cinnéide starred in an emphatic win as Jack O'Connor led Kerry to his first title as manager.

Two years later, Mayo stunned Dublin the last four with Ciaran McDonald landing a sublime winner, but it was the same old story in the final as an early goal blitz paved the way for another handsome win for Kerry.

While O'Connor stood down at the end of 2006, Pat O'Shea would guide them to another title title the following season - the last time Kerry achieved back to back All-Irelands, only for Tyrone to deny them three-in-a-row the following year - a repeat of the 2005 decider.

As that great Kerry team's powers began to fade by the end of the decade, Mayo would find a new nemesis as after defeat by Donegal in 2012, Dublin would account for them in the 2013 decider, again in 2016 after a replay that was largely down to two first-half own goals in the drawn game, while Dean Rock would break their hearts with a winning free at the death in the 2017 final.

However, Kerry and Mayo would serve up some incredible semi-final drama in the 2010s as after Kieran O'Leary salvaged a draw for Kerry at Croke Park, the Kingdom would win after extra-time in a thriller at Limerick's Gaelic Grounds.

Three years later at the same stage, it was roles reversed as Paddy Durcan rescued a draw for Mayo who finished the job in the replay thanks to goals from current manager Andy Moran and Diarmuid O'Connor.

While the counties lost two All-Ireland finals apiece since that game, Kerry have added two more titles in the third coming of O'Connor.

They sides swapped wins in 2022 and 2023, Kerry now an established force led by the talents of the Cliffords, the Geaneys, Gavin White and Sean O'Shea.

Mayo contain many survivors of their most recent final defeat by Tyrone in 2021, but a fresh crop have also emerged in Kobe McDonald, Darragh Beirne, Eoin McGreal and Cian McHale.

Will the ghosts of All-Ireland finals past continue to haunt Mayo and Kerry cement their place at the top, or will the 75 years of hurt finally come to an end against a county that has handed them three of those 11 defeats since 1951?

Sunday will be a day to remember for one set of supporters, while the other will revisit that sense of devastation both know only too well on All-Ireland final day.

As for the 'curse'? Well, the last member of the Mayo 1951 panel, Dr Mick Loftus, passed away in 2023.
