title: Sen. Peters wants to know why ICE bought spyware that can take control of phones
description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has purchased commercial spyware that can covertly take control of phones, collect messages, photos and location information.
fullText:
Washington — The ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee is demanding that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement explain why it has purchased commercial spyware capable of covertly taking control of phones as well as collecting messages, photographs, location information and other personal data.

Democratic Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan called the purchase "one of the most significant expansions of DHS and ICE's surveillance ambitions to date," flagging potential civil liberties concerns and risks to U.S. national security. Peters sought clarity from Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin in a letter exclusively obtained by CBS News and dated July 23, calling into question ICE's $2 million, sole-source purchase of Graphite, a surveillance tool developed by Paragon Solutions and now owned by REDLattice.

"Misuse of Graphite is not hypothetical," Peters wrote, mentioning public reporting that more than 90 journalists and civil society members were targeted by the technology across several countries.

While the senator from Michigan does not allege that ICE has used Graphite against journalists, protesters or other Americans, Peters demanded the agency disclose whether the software has been deployed domestically, who has been targeted and legal authority supporting use of the tool.

The ranking member said he was "deeply troubled about how Graphite might be used in the United States to target Americans," pointing to ongoing concerns about ICE's collection of information involving protests, social media posts and other First Amendment-protected activities.

Peters also asked ICE for the number of U.S. and non-U.S. people who have been targeted, where they were located and why the software was procured. He also requested information about whether the data collected by Graphite has been shared with other government agencies, companies or nonprofit organizations.

The lengthy inquiry seeks contracts, privacy assessments, civil rights reviews, security policies and records connected to a September 2024 agreement, an October 2024 stop-work order and the contract's later reactivation in August 2025.

In his letter, Peters said his committee staff had requested briefings from the Department of Homeland Security in December 2025 and from ICE in January 2026, but never heard back substantively.

The ranking member requested an immediate briefing and gave ICE until Aug. 7 to provide documents and answer questions about the spyware's use, oversight and security. Because Democrats do not control Congress, Peters is not able to order ICE to comply with his demands — he may only request information.

CBS News has reached out to ICE, Graphite and RedLattice for comment.

A senior DHS official told CBS News that the department and ICE are "[e]mploying various forms of technology in support of investigations and law enforcement activities aids in the arrest of criminal gang members, child sex offenders, murderers, drug dealers, identity thieves and more, all while respecting civil liberties and privacy interests."

title: CNN host admits he was wrong to say illegal immigrant voting 'never happens' after New Jersey error
description: Michael Smerconish says he can no longer claim noncitizen voting never happens after New Jersey revealed a software error registered 6,600 noncitizens.
fullText:
CNN and SiriusXM host Michael Smerconish acknowledged Wednesday on "The Michael Smerconish Program" that he could no longer claim noncitizen voting never occurred after New Jersey disclosed that a software error improperly registered roughly 6,600 noncitizens and fewer than 400 cast ballots.

"I can't say that any longer," Smerconish said. "I don't know how often it does happen, but I can't say any longer, 'This never happens.'"

Smerconish said he had previously reached the opposite conclusion after discussing a January New York Times analysis titled "Initial Review Finds No Widespread Illegal Voting by Migrants, Puncturing a Trump Claim." The analysis found no evidence of widespread fraud but noted that noncitizens sometimes appeared on voter rolls.

Smerconish said the New Jersey disclosure would give President Donald Trump and his allies a lasting response when opponents disputed that noncitizen voting occurred.

Gop Erupts Over 6,600 Noncitizen Voters Found In Blue State As Scandal Deepens: 'Worse Than Anyone Expected'

"'Well, what about New Jersey?' See, it actually does happen," Smerconish said, in a clip flagged by Mediaite.

Political analyst Mark Halperin agreed that the disclosure undercut categorical claims about noncitizen voting while cautioning that more information was needed before conclusions could be reached about its scale.

"Based on what we now know, the thing that Democrats said doesn't happen happened," Halperin said. "And it's not right to take the word of the Democratic governor of New Jersey about what actually happened."

Halperin called for an independent investigation into how the registrations occurred, whether the same problem appeared elsewhere and whether New Jersey's estimate captured the full extent of the error.

Watch: Trump Doj Vows To Pursue 'Every Single' Voting Violation After Nj Roll Shocker

"If it happened by accident on this small scale, it requires a lot more explanation and investigation about whether it's happened in New Jersey more or elsewhere," Halperin said. "But the scale is not very significant. So we need to know more."

Fox News Digital reached out to New Jersey Gov. Mike Sherrill for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Sherrill said the error affected people who indicated they were not U.S. citizens while applying for driver's licenses or identification cards between June 2023 and June 2024. The system nevertheless registered them to vote.

"Our preliminary analysis shows fewer than 400 individuals who were newly registered for the first time because of the error voted," Sherrill said. "They were registered as Democrats, Republicans and Unaffiliated voters and were scattered across the state."

New Jersey Removes 6,600 People From Voter Rolls Who Were Eligible To Cast A Ballot For 2024 Election

Sherrill ordered the affected registrations removed, launched an investigation and began replacing IDEMIA, the vendor involved with the Motor Vehicle Commission system. She blamed failures under former Democratic Gov. Phil Murphy's administration.

Click Here For More Coverage Of Media And Culture

"This failure didn't occur under my watch, but accountability starts now," Sherrill said.

IDEMIA disputed efforts to place responsibility solely on the company, telling Fox News Digital that New Jersey election officials were responsible for determining eligibility.

"The voter registration information is transmitted to the New Jersey Department of State, Division of Elections, which is ultimately responsible for verifying eligibility to vote," IDEMIA said.

The Justice Department subsequently demanded information about the 6,600 registrations and the fewer than 400 people who voted. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon gave the state five days to provide names, registration details and voting records.

"Ensuring that U.S. citizens' votes are not illegally diluted by noncitizens' votes is of paramount importance," Dhillon said.

title: Barcelona confirm huge Frenkie de Jong knee injury blow
description: Barcelona have been dealt an early setback ahead of the 2026/27 season after confirming that midfielder Frenkie de Jong has suffered a knee injury that will keep him out for several weeks.The Spanish ...
fullText:
Barcelona have been dealt an early setback ahead of the 2026/27 season after confirming that midfielder Frenkie de Jong has suffered a knee injury that will keep him out for several weeks.

The Spanish club announced that the Netherlands international has torn the medial collateral ligament in his right knee.

While Barcelona did not provide a specific timeline for his return, the good news is that the injury will not require surgery. He will begin a rehabilitation program and hope to return as soon as possible.

The injury was discovered after several medical examinations carried out over the past few days.

De Jong had already been dealing with discomfort while on international duty at the World Cup, where he was often seen wearing a protective bandage on his right knee.

After the tournament, De Jong was given extra time off and visited Barcelona’s training facilities earlier this week to undergo further checks, leading to the final diagnosis.

The news is a major disappointment for Barcelona manager Hansi Flick, who had hoped to start the campaign with one of his most experienced midfielders available.

De Jong was a crucial player for Barcelona last season, making 38 appearances across all competitions.

He scored just once but weighed in with eight assists. He also averaged two interceptions, 2.3 tackles, 2.3 clearances, and five ball recoveries per 90 minutes.

De Jong also won half of his aerial duels and came out on top in 59% of his ground battles.

Despite losing such an important player, Barcelona are not expected to make any changes to their transfer plans. They believe they have the quality and depth in midfield to cope with De Jong’s absence.

Barcelona are also moving ahead with their transfer plans, with the club working on a potential exit for Marc Casado rather than searching for a replacement for De Jong.

De Jong’s latest injury continues a frustrating run of fitness problems.

Over the past two seasons, he has struggled with several setbacks, including a serious ankle issue and a thigh injury that sidelined him for nearly two months last season.

title: 76ers reportedly signing $147M elite shooter, ex-Lakers NBA champion to reunite with LeBron James
description: The Philadelphia 76ers were able to land LeBron James on Friday morning. They are apparently not wasting anytime to build the bench behind James, bringing in his former teammate that won a NBA championship together.
fullText:
76ers reportedly signing $147M elite shooter, ex-Lakers NBA champion to reunite with LeBron James originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Philadelphia 76ers were not considered a serious contender for LeBron James when NBA free agency began nearly a month ago. However, after making an aggressive trade for former Boston Celtic Jaylen Brown, Philadelphia opened up an entirely new opportunity for the organization.

After James remained quiet for more than three weeks, the decision was finalized Friday morning when he announced that he would finish his career in Philadelphia.

“LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for his final run at another NBA championship, he announced Friday,” ESPN’s Dave McMenamin wrote. “James, 41, is signing a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania.”

The 76ers already have an impressive starting lineup and solid depth, but they could still look to add more pieces to the roster. One specific area of need is adding more defensive-minded players and reliable three-point shooters off the bench.

“The Philadelphia 76ers should prioritize defense and three-point shooting after LeBron James signed with the team this offseason,” Athlon Sports’ Paolo Songco wrote.

The 76ers are undoubtedly one of the favorites to win the Eastern Conference this upcoming season. Their roster is loaded with talent and difficult to overlook. It also does not appear that Philadelphia is finished making moves, as James’ former teammate Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is expected to join the team once he is officially bought out by the Memphis Grizzlies.

“Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is negotiating a buyout with the Grizzlies and intends to sign with the 76ers, per Chris B Haynes. KCP joins Bron in Philly,” Bleacher Report posted.

Caldwell-Pope is exactly the type of player the 76ers need off the bench, and he brings a wealth of championship experience. James and Caldwell-Pope won a championship together with the Los Angeles Lakers during the 2020 NBA bubble.

Caldwell-Pope has earned $147 million through his NBA contracts throughout his career. This is the type of move Philadelphia should make, and it is one James will certainly approve of. So far, after landing James, the 76ers are making all the right moves.

title: La Masia stars steal the show as Barcelona register first pre-season win over CE Europa
description: Barcelona opened their pre-season campaign with an encouraging 4-1 victory over CE Europa, but apart from the scoreline, the match belonged to La Masia as a host of young talents impressed Hansi Flick...
fullText:
Barcelona opened their pre-season campaign with an encouraging 4-1 victory over CE Europa, but apart from the scoreline, the match belonged to La Masia as a host of young talents impressed Hansi Flick in the club’s first friendly of the summer.

Having returned to training on July 13, the match offered Barcelona players their first opportunity to build fitness ahead of the new season.

As expected, the German coach relied heavily on youngsters and reserve-team players, using the game to assess individual performances rather than chase a convincing result.

Goals from Ibrahim Diarra, Hector Fort, Ebrima Tunkara and Alex Gonzalez sealed a comfortable win behind closed doors, giving Flick plenty of positives to take from his side’s opening outing.

The friendly match showcased the strength of Barcelona’s academy, with several homegrown players making the most of their opportunity.

As such, Diarra opened the scoring before Fort added another as Barcelona established control early on.

Barcelona registered a commanding win over CE Europa. (Picture credit: Instagram/@fcbarcelona)

Tunkara and Alex Gonzalez also found the net to complete an impressive team display, underlining the quality emerging from La Masia.

Although Barcelona were clearly the better side throughout, the coaching staff’s main focus was never the final result.

Instead, the priority was to build match fitness, assess the squad’s physical condition, and allow several young players to experience senior football under Flick.

With many established first-team players unavailable, the encounter provided valuable minutes for footballers hoping to strengthen their case before the competitive campaign begins.

One of the biggest talking points from Barcelona’s first pre-season friendly was Flick’s decision to give opportunities to players whose futures remain unresolved this summer.

Four La Masia players were on the scoresheet. (Picture credit: Instagram/@fcbarcelona)

Marc Casado, Marc-Andre ter Stegen and Roony Bardghji were all involved even though their futures are uncertain.

Furthermore, New signing Karim Adeyemi was not included in the matchday group.

Having only completed his first training session with his new teammates earlier in the day, the coaching staff felt it was too soon to hand the German winger his unofficial debut.

Lastly, Ronald Araujo and Alejandro Balde also missed the fixture, while Marc Bernal was left out after experiencing minor discomfort.

Barcelona chose not to take any unnecessary risks with the youngster at such an early stage of pre-season.

title: Liverpool eyeing move for £77m Mohamed Salah successor
description: Mohamed Salah exiting Liverpool is probably going to be the biggest story to emerge from Anfield this summer. The Egyptian King was at least expected to see out his two-year extension with the Reds bu...
fullText:
Mohamed Salah exiting Liverpool is probably going to be the biggest story to emerge from Anfield this summer.

The Egyptian King was at least expected to see out his two-year extension with the Reds but, after hardly being used by Arne Slot, he decided enough was enough and had his contract mutually terminated.

This has led to fans going into a meltdown about who Liverpool could sign to replace him and why his successor hasn't been brought in yet.

Indeed, the Reds have added a couple of new players to their ranks already but, with Chelsea signing Morgan Rogers for £117 million and Manchester City signing Elliott Anderson for £116 million, it feels like Liverpool need to make some serious moves soon.

So, the fact that rumours linking Liverpool with one of their former targets have re-emerged surely means that some movement is going to occur soon, right?

At the moment, the market for wingers seems quite underwhelming.

Yan Diomande or Antoine Semenyo were the perfect players for Liverpool to target but, since Diomande is going to Paris Saint-Germain and Semenyo joined Man City in January, those options are now off the table.

This has lad to many questions emerging from Anfield with some fans even wondering whether Federico Chiesa could be handed a regular starting role by Iraola.

However, if Liverpool want to get back to their best, they need to make a marquee signing that can more or less help carry their attack, especially since Hugo Ekitike is still out injured.

And now, a fresh update from Ekrem Konur has given Liverpool's fanbase just a little bit of hope that a marquee attacker can be brought to L4 soon.

"Liverpool are interested in Nico Williams, but Arsenal’s pursuit is currently more advanced," he wrote via his personal X account.

"Arsenal have made new contacts for the Athletic Club winger, with sporting director Andrea Berta assessing whether a deal is feasible.

"His contract includes a £77M release clause, a figure Arsenal and several Premier League clubs can realistically meet.

"Nico Williams is back on Arsenal’s shortlist."

Iraola will want to get his team back to their best as soon as possible.

Everyone involved with Liverpool knows that the 2025-26 season was far from acceptable.

Slot failed to play to the strengths of his players and seemed to turn his back on all of the Reds' academy prospects who probably deserved a chance more than some of his first-team regulars.

title: Bangladesh captain hails Australia's decision to name a full-strength Test squad as an 'achievement' for Bangladesh cricket
description: Bangladesh Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto believes Australia naming a full-strength squad with Cummins, Starc, and Smith is an achievement for the Tigers.
fullText:
Bangladesh captain hails Australia's decision to name a full-strength Test squad as an 'achievement' for Bangladesh cricket originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Najmul Shanto calls Australia's full-strength squad for Test series as an achievement for Bangladesh cricket.

Bangladesh face injury worries: Litton Das, Nahid Rana, and Shoriful Islam are all sidelined.

The two-match series begins August 13 in Darwin, Australia.

Bangladesh Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto declared on Friday that he doesn't sense any complacency from Australia ahead of their upcoming two-Test series, set to begin in Darwin on August 13, and instead claimed that the hosts' team selection reflects genuine respect for his side.

Australia have opted to field their strongest available Test line-up for the series, a decision Shanto himself labelled an "achievement" for Bangladeshi cricket. The visiting side will contend with a battle-tested pace unit comprising Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Scott Boland, backed by the experience of veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon.

On the batting front, Australia's order carries serious weight through Steve Smith, Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head, while all-rounders Cameron Green and Beau Webster round out a squad with considerable depth in both departments.

Speaking to reporters at the Notun Kuri final ceremony held at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium, Shanto addressed questions about the historic tour, noting that he had never previously witnessed anything quite like this in Bangladesh's cricketing history.

"Normally, I have never seen anything like this before in Bangladesh cricket. When teams play against us, there are usually a lot of experiments. I would say this is an achievement for our team," Shanto told reporters.

"Because they have brought such a team, it is a very big opportunity for us to see how well we can play cricket against them. I would say we have already managed to build a good position with this Test team. Because if you look at the opposition squad, it is clear that they have not taken this series lightly."

MORE: Australia squad for Bangladesh Test series 2026: Full team list for AUS vs BAN red-ball series

Bangladesh's build-up to the tour hasn't been entirely smooth, however, with several fitness concerns casting a shadow over squad planning.

Wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das, who has been in fine form recently, remains sidelined by a calf injury picked up back in June. He travelled to Singapore over the weekend for scans aimed at better understanding the injury's severity.

"Yet to heal, but staying positive. Grateful for the medical care and attention in Singapore, though. Keep me in your prayers," Litton wrote on his official Facebook page.

Litton isn't the only bowler or batter facing fitness hurdles. Fast bowler Nahid Rana, who impressed during Bangladesh's recent ODI series win over Zimbabwe, suffered a side strain in the second T20I of that same series. Reports suggest the 23-year-old is running short on time to be fully fit for the Australia series.

Fellow pacer Shoriful Islam also picked up a hamstring problem during the Zimbabwe series, though there's more optimism around his recovery timeline, with sources suggesting he could be available in time for the second and final Test.

MORE: India vs Bangladesh series put in doubt after latest BCB media rights delay

The string of pace-bowling injuries has prompted some criticism suggesting Bangladesh's team management could have handled their fast bowlers' workloads more carefully.

Shanto, however, was careful to distance himself from those decisions, explaining that such calls fall under the responsibility of the physiotherapy and training staff rather than the playing group, and that there wasn't much more he could add beyond that.

"Those decisions (judging players' workload management and injury issues) are actually taken by the physio, the trainer and the management group, and they are managing it that way. Beyond that, there is not much more to say," Shanto said.

Test cricket outside the sport's traditional powerhouses often gets treated as an afterthought, with the big four teams routinely rotating squads or resting key players against so-called weaker opposition.

Australia choosing to field their strongest available eleven against Bangladesh signals a shift worth acknowledging, even if it's driven partly by World Test Championship points rather than pure goodwill.

For a Bangladesh side that has long fought for credibility on the international stage, facing Smith, Starc and company at full strength offers a genuine measuring stick rather than a hollow contest against a second-string outfit.

That said, the timing couldn't be worse given Bangladesh's mounting injury list heading into the series. Playing a full-strength Australia while missing key contributors like Litton Das and Nahid Rana risks turning a meaningful opportunity into a lopsided contest before a ball is even bowled. Respect from the opposition means little if Bangladesh can’t field their best possible side to match it.

title: NBA superstar LeBron James to join Philadelphia 76ers
description: Basketball superstar LeBron James announces he will join the Philadelphia 76ers for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.
fullText:
LeBron James has announced he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers next season for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.

The 41-year-old, the highest points scorer in the history of the league, left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight years last month.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat were also rumoured to be in the running for the four-time NBA champion.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fanbase and start this incredible journey one last time," James said on X.

James has won an NBA title with all three teams he previously played for. He won two with Miami, who earlier this week mistakenly posted a link to an 'introductory press conference' for James.

A Heat spokesperson told Reuters the video was posted in error by staff who were preparing for the possibility of James rejoining the team he played for between 2010 and 2014.

Either side of that Miami stint, James had two spells with Cleveland, who drafted James in 2003 and are based near his hometown of Akron, Ohio.

"Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always [be] home," James added.

James helped the Cavs become NBA champions in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2018, claiming another NBA title two years later.

He has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, all between 2009 and 2013, and has been an NBA All-Star the last 22 seasons running.

'Maybe he's a racist' - Trump critical of James

James said after last season that he was "pretty sure I [had] played my last game" but realised "I still truly love this game and I have more to give".

ESPN has reported that James has signed a two-year contract, with a player option for the second year, worth $8m (£6m). His average salary with the Lakers last season was $50.7m (£38m).

James added: "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point?

"I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

The 76ers reached the Conference semi-finals in last season's play-offs, where they lost to the eventual champions, the New York Knicks.

They have since acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics, in exchange for Paul George and some future draft picks.

title: Jose Mourinho’s first Real Madrid training match offers early glimpse of new era
description: Real Madrid took another step in Jose Mourinho’s pre-season preparations by holding their first training match of the summer against Alcorcon.There was obvious curiosity about how the Portuguese tac...
fullText:
Real Madrid took another step in Jose Mourinho’s pre-season preparations by holding their first training match of the summer against Alcorcon.

There was obvious curiosity about how the Portuguese tactician would set his team up and a desire to observe and identify early key patterns.

According to MARCA, the afternoon at the Alfredo Di Stefano Stadium gave supporters an early look at Mourinho’s methods, his coaching staff and the first tactical ideas taking shape ahead of the new campaign.

The session started with fitness work led jointly by Antonio Pintus and Antonio Dias, Mourinho’s long-time fitness coach.

Los Blancos players have suffered so many injuries in recent seasons, and their collaboration is expected to help put some of those issues behind them.

After the warm-up, the players moved into rondos directed by assistant coach Joao Tralhao before Mourinho took a more active role during the practice match.

Real Madrid registered a 1-0 win over Alcorcon. (Picture credit: Instagram/@realmadrid)

The Portuguese coach’s first starting line-up featured Andriy Lunin in goal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Raul Asencio, Dean Huijsen and Alvaro Carreras in defence, Eduardo Camavinga, Cestero and Arda Guler in midfield, with Franco Mastantuono, Gonzalo Garcia and academy forward Gabri Valero leading the attack.

The standout performer was Mastantuono, who looked lively throughout the opening period.

The Argentine won an early penalty after a direct run, although Arda Guler was unable to convert from the spot as Madrid’s penalty struggles continued.

At a time when Mastantuono’s future at the club is not clear and a loan deal could be on the cards, this was an important display from the Argentine youngster.

The match eventually finished 1-0 in Madrid’s favour after Daniel Yanez converted a later penalty.

Trent Alexander-Arnold started under Mourinho. (Picture credit: Instagram/@realmadrid)

First-team players completed around 70 minutes before youth-team players took over for the remainder of the session.

Off the pitch, Federico Valverde, Rodrygo and Eder Militao watched from the stands as they continued their own preparations, while Ferland Mendy remains in recovery alongside Militao and Rodrygo.

Pre-season training matches are never the place for definitive conclusions, yet they often provide useful clues about a coach’s priorities.

Mastantuono’s confidence, the involvement of several Castilla prospects and Mourinho’s willingness to experiment were all visible.

Obviously, some of this is bound to change once the World Cup stars start returning to the fold, but Mourinho’s Madrid are off to a winning start and, for now, that counts for something.

title: Hansi Flick loses faith in Barcelona captain as summer exit becomes real possibility
description: Frenkie de Jong’s future at Barcelona has taken an unexpected twist after fresh reports suggest Hansi Flick is no longer convinced the Dutch midfielder should remain a key part of his plans.Accordin...
fullText:
Frenkie de Jong’s future at Barcelona has taken an unexpected twist after fresh reports suggest Hansi Flick is no longer convinced the Dutch midfielder should remain a key part of his plans.

According to Gerard Romero, the Barcelona manager has grown increasingly unconvinced by De Jong’s recent performances and overall role within the squad.

As a result, the club could now consider offers for the midfielder if the right proposal arrives before the transfer window closes.

The development comes just days after reports claimed that the relationship between Flick and De Jong had deteriorated, raising questions over the long-term future of one of Barcelona’s most experienced players.

The uncertainty surrounding Frenkie de Jong’s Barcelona future stretches back to the closing stages of last season, when trust between the midfielder and his manager began to fade.

Frenkie de Jong was injured during the World Cup. (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz/Getty Images)

Barcelona are currently monitoring De Jong’s recovery from the knee injury he suffered during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, but concerns over his future are no longer linked solely to his fitness.

As reported before, the turning point came during Barcelona’s UEFA Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid in the 2025/26 season.

De Jong had been cleared by Barcelona’s medical staff to start the match and was expected to play around an hour.

However, despite receiving medical approval, the Dutch international is said to have decided against featuring, preferring not to take any unnecessary risks.

That decision significantly changed Flick’s opinion of the midfielder, with the relationship between the pair deteriorating from that point onwards.

Barcelona are open to selling Frenkie de Jong. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

The latest information from Gerard Romero suggests Barcelona are no longer completely opposed to the idea of selling the midfielder.

This means if a suitable offer arrives during the summer transfer window, the club could be prepared to part ways with De Jong, marking a significant shift in stance compared to previous windows when he was considered untouchable.

The Dutchman remains one of the senior figures in the dressing room, but his current knee injury has already left Barcelona waiting for clarity over his return.

Now, uncertainty over his place in Flick’s long-term plans has only added more tension to the situation.

title: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope negotiating buy out from Grizzlies, to sign with 76ers
description: KCP reunites with LeBron James, the two of them won a title together in Los Angeles.
fullText:
Kentavious Caldwell-Pope won his first ring next to LeBron James, now he is headed to Philadelphia to try and do it again.

Caldwell-Pope and the Grizzlies are working out a buyout, and once the veteran wing clears waivers, he intends to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, reports NBA insider Chris Haynes.

KCP moving on from Memphis is not a surprise. He was brought in while the team still had Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. and was looking to win. With the Grizzlies pivoting to a youth movement — plus they are dealing with a roster crunch — it makes sense to buy out KCP, who is set to make $ 21.6 million this season. (KCP likely gives the Grizzlies a discount of exactly how much he can sign with the 76ers for.)

Caldwell-Pope was a key part of the Lakers' title run in the bubble, and three years later became a starter for the Denver team that won a title behind Nikola Jokic.

However, the past couple of seasons his game has slipped. Last season in Memphis, he averaged just 8.4 points a game and shot 31.6% from 3-point range. He was out from February on after having surgery to adjust a misaligned pinky finger on his right hand.

Philadelphia has a little roster work to do to bring in LeBron and KCP, including clearing a roster spot or two. The 76ers are not far enough under their first-apron hard cap to sign the two veterans, even at the minimum, which means more roster moves are coming. Dalen Terry and his non-guaranteed contract are almost certain to be let go. Jabari Walker also has a non-guaranteed contract, but there are other moves the team could make to bring in the two veterans.

This is another loss for Miami, which had its eyes on KCP as well.

title: Report: Liverpool eyeing Luis Diaz regen in £51m ‘crown jewel’; contact made with his camp
description: Liverpool have been named among a host of top European clubs showing an interest in a highly coveted winger who could potentially be their next Luis Diaz.The Colombian was signed from FC Porto in Janu...
fullText:
Liverpool have been named among a host of top European clubs showing an interest in a highly coveted winger who could potentially be their next Luis Diaz.

The Colombian was signed from FC Porto in January 2022 for an initial £37.5m (BBC Sport), instantly becoming an idol of the Kop with his dynamism in attack and going on to score 41 goals in 148 appearances at Anfield before leaving for Bayern Munich last year.

Fast forward to July 2026, and the Reds are on the lookout for wide attacking reinforcements as they enter life without Mo Salah, with Bradley Barcola and Maghnes Akliouche seemingly among their primary targets, and they also appear to have their eyes on a teenage talent currently playing in Portugal.

According to a report for Fussballdaten, Liverpool are joined by both Manchester clubs, Arsenal, Chelsea, Newcastle, Bayern Munich and Atletico Madrid in monitoring Porto winger Oskar Pietuszewski.

It’s Borussia Dortmund who appear to be leading the chase for now, having contacted the 18-year-old’s representatives and presented a ‘clear development plan’ outlining his planned progression to the first team. The Bundesliga side are understood to be planning an opening offer of €35m (£29.8m).

However, the Portuguese champions are determined to keep hold of the teenager and aren’t prepared to accept any offers short of his €60m (£51.2m) release clause.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Liverpool potentially recruiting Pietuszewski would have echoes of the Diaz swoop in 2022, with the latter being signed from Porto, and the two wingers also boast stylistic comparisons.

GOAL writer James Westwood noted how both players have similar qualities in terms of their agile footwork, with reference also made to the 18-year-old’s ‘lightning acceleration and shooting power’ and his ‘warrior’s mentality’.

A tactical analysis for Driblab described him as ‘the crown jewel of Polish youth football’ and highlighted his penchant for drawing free kicks with his electrifying dribbling ability – not unlike Rio Ngumoha.

However, despite impression for Porto since his January move from Jagiellonia Bialystok, Pietuszewski wouldn’t be a standout candidate for what Liverpool need right now.

He plays primarily on the left flank, where the Reds are already well stocked (in contrast to a lack of depth on the right), while his goal return at senior level leaves plenty of room for improvement (just seven in 72 games).

Also, he’d be a signing for the long-term rather than the here-and-now, and it’s the latter that LFC really need at this moment.

On that basis, it’d be difficult to justify spending more than £50m on him, although the scale of transfer interest in him indicates just how high a ceiling he could have in years to come.

title: A city's letter to a distant king
description: As the franchise turns the page from LeBron James to Luka Dončić—a player who embodies the passion and blue-collar grit this town craves—the message to Philadelphia is clear: you've been warned, and from Los Angeles, it's good riddance and goodbye.
fullText:
Now that you've officially taken your talents to Philadelphia—your fourth stop, your "last decision," your two-year, $8-million victory lap—Laker fans across the globe can finally exhale.

The eight-year experiment is over. And we have a confession to make: from Watts to Westwood, we never wanted you.

Let's be honest about what you were. You were a mercenary, not a Laker. A hired gun who wore purple and gold but never bled it.

Fred Roggin said it best: "He wore a Laker uniform, but he wasn't a Laker. I always felt that way. I think with LeBron, it's about LeBron." Byron Scott, a man who actually earned his place in Lakers lore, agreed—you're "not a true Laker."

You like going "off script," Scott said. Translation: you were never willing to buy into what it means to be a Laker.

You were always LeBron first, Laker a distant second.

You never ingratiated yourself with this city, and at times it seemed the team, even after the Lakers drafted your son.

Outside of moonlighting at the Drew League and Kendrick Lamar's Pop Out event, you were invisible. You didn't go past the 10 freeway unless it was for practice.

There was little mystique or murmurs about you supporting local businesses, surprising ill children at the Children's Hospital or just exploring outside of the confines of your Westside bubble.

When the Lakers hosted children at the practice facility for Christmas, your presence was noticeably absent.

When this city was grieving Kobe Bryant—a man who was Los Angeles—you took the floor in that first game back, conjured up fake tears and you lost—127-119 to the Portland Trail Blazers.

When you broke the NBA's all-time scoring record, you lost that game too.

When the city needed you to put the team on your back and carry it like Kobe would have, you came up short.

You hijacked our franchise the way you hijacked every other one.

Cleveland. Miami. Cleveland again.

Throughout your career, you left a trail of scorched earth, pressured organizations to trade away futures and quit when things got difficult. You did the same to us.

Two of your Lakers teams missed the playoffs entirely—2018-19 and 2021-22.

Yes, you delivered one championship, and even that one—the 2020 bubble ring—rings hollow.

In a city accustomed to championships won by the pair—Magic and Kareem, Shaq and Kobe—your lone title feels like a footnote, not a legacy.

In your career, you've squandered more talent than any great could imagine.

Let's talk about the Hall of Famers you've played beside. Dwyane Wade. Kyrie Irving. Anthony Davis. Chris Bosh. Ray Allen. Kevin Love. Russell Westbrook. Carmelo Anthony. Shaquille O'Neal. Dwight Howard. And now, Luka Dončić.

Yet somehow, despite all that talent, you underachieved as a Laker. You went 4-6 in your last 10 playoff games as a Laker.

Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James (23) reacts after a play against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the first half during game two of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Paycom Center.

Underachieved doesn't even begin to cover it.

Some of us saw the hidden hand.

We watched Klutch Sports manipulate narratives through beat writers gawking at an opportunity to breathe your air in hopes of a story, pressure the front office, and meddle with the roster.

Rich Paul's influence poisoned the locker room—remember when he floated trading Austin Reaves?

The organization grew frustrated with the "outsized ego" and the control Klutch exerted over basketball decisions. You weren't just a player; you were a shadow GM, and the franchise suffered for it.

Your first game as a Laker told us everything.

I was there. I saw it with my own eyes in the bowels of the arena.

You chose your friend Chris Paul over the teammates, Rajon Rondo and Brandon Ingram, who literally fought beside you in that very game. That decision fractured the locker room from Day One.

It set the tone for your entire tenure: LeBron's circle, LeBron's interests, LeBron's agenda—everyone else be damned.

The "Church of Bron," the "LBJ community," made it impossible to cheer for you.

Every win was because of you. Every loss was because you "needed more help." You poisoned the fanbase with that entitlement. You made it exhausting to be a Laker fan, because rooting for the team meant defending your every move, every failure, every excuse.

You failed to etch many indelible moments as you sat on your Los Angeles throne. You are, at best, a third-tier Laker.

Behind Magic, Kareem, Kobe, Shaq, West, Baylor, Worthy, Pau Gasol, and for some, Nick Van Exel and Eddie Jones. Although you'll be immortalized there, you don't belong in the rafters. You don't deserve a statue.

Not in the house Kobe built, not in Los Angeles.

You wore the uniform, but you were never one of us.

Rob Pelinka was blessed to be gifted Luka Dončić.

He embodies the blue-collar ethos of this city. He plays with fight and passion—the kind of gritty, never-say-die basketball this town was built on.

He's paid to have defaced Kobe murals restored. He takes time after practices to talk to staff, joke with equipment managers and acknowledge the people who keep the team running.

Lakers staff have shared stories of his humility, his genuine respect for everyone in the organization. He leads through consistency, not ego. He's everything you were not.

Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James (23) reacts after he is fouled during the first half in game four of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Crypto.com Arena.

Now, a warning to Philadelphia.

Philly, we wish you well—but you have no idea what you're getting. You're getting the same LeBron who hijacked three franchises before us. The same LeBron who will demand control, trade away your future, and make everything about him. Look at his free agency approach––the time, the stories, the drama.

You're inheriting the same LeBron who, when things get hard, will look for the exit.

And Church of Bron? You think the Los Angeles media coddled him? Wait until he faces the Philadelphia media.

They will not protect him. They will not insulate him. They will not carry water for Klutch Sports. When he fails to meet their expectations—and with Joel Embiid's injury history and a thin roster behind him, he will—they will eat him alive.

The criticism, the accountability, the vitriol—it will be relentless. And there will be no Laker legacy to hide behind. No warm California sunshine to soften the blow. Just cold, hard Philadelphia reality.

You came, you conquered nothing and you left.

And Laker Nation is better for it.

title: A summer defining moment has arrived for Manchester City as Real Madrid eye their midfield general
description: The future of Rodri has been a hot topic ever since the 2026 World Cup ended. All week Rodri has been linked with a summer move to La Liga giants, while Manchester City were hoping to extend Rodri’s...
fullText:
The future of Rodri has been a hot topic ever since the 2026 World Cup ended. All week Rodri has been linked with a summer move to La Liga giants, while Manchester City were hoping to extend Rodri’s contract. Now it has been reported that Real Madrid do indeed hope to sign Manchester City’s midfield general this summer. All of a sudden, a summer defining moment has landed at Manchester City’s doorstep.

David Ornstein and Mario Cortegana have reported for The Athletic that Real Madrid are aiming to sign Rodri this summer. Furthermore, it is reported that Real Madrid are confident of securing the Ballon d’Or-winning midfielder. It is also reported that as yet no direct talks have taken place between Manchester City and Real Madrid over a deal for Rodri. It is also included in The Athletic report that Manchester City are hopeful that Rodri will see out the final year of his contract. However, Rodri has previously expressed his wish to return to Spain and now Real Madrid are determined to make Rodri’s wish come true this summer.

A fork in the moment has arrived for Manchester City in the summer transfer window. David Ornstein and Mario Cortegana’s report illustrates that Real Madrid do indeed want to sign Rodri this summer. Rodri’s wish to one day play for the La Liga giants is by now well-established. City now have a decision to make assuming that Real Madrid can satisfy City’s asking price to sell the World Cup winner.

Does Manchester City hold Rodri to the final year of his contract? Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. A fully fit Rodri turns City from a very good side into an elite side. Selling Rodri would create a sizable void in Manchester City’s midfield and in their leadership. Is that something City are willing to allow to occur? That answer isn’t immediately clear but the fact that Rodri is so important to City may provide that particular answer.

The other side to the coin is whether Manchester City keeps a player who clearly wants to leave the club. Typically, besides Bernardo Silva, City do not keep players who wish to leave. This is the situation that they find themselves in with Rodri. It is no secret that Rodri wants to a move to Real Madrid. That has been obvious since the World Cup concluded. Perhaps Rodri’s time at City has naturally concluded as he has nothing left to achieve at the club. He has scaled every mountain.

Do the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders want to keep player, no matter how important they are, who doesn’t want to be there? The answer to that particular question, has the potential to massively alter City’s summer transfer window plans.

Manchester City have seemingly reached a defining moment this summer. Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. Real Madrid now want to sign him, and he wants a move back to Spain. Whatever City decides to do with Rodri will define their summer. It is that big, and hopefully a decision one way or another comes quickly so City can plan for what lies ahead with or without Rodri.

title: Report: Chelsea star could be set to leave in £30m deal
description: Chelsea Transfer News: Como Push for Trevoh Chalobah Deal as Talks ContinueComo remain firmly in the race for Trevoh Chalobah, with fresh talks scheduled with Chelsea on Saturday 25 July as the clubs ...
fullText:
Como remain firmly in the race for Trevoh Chalobah, with fresh talks scheduled with Chelsea on Saturday 25 July as the clubs attempt to reach a final agreement over the defender’s future. According to Sky Italia, discussions are ongoing and the key issue continues to centre on the structure of the fee.

The broad outline of the negotiations is clear. Chelsea want £30m guaranteed to sanction Chalobah’s departure, while Como are currently holding at around £25m, with a preference for part of the package to be tied to appearances and performance-related objectives. That gap is not vast, but it remains significant enough to prevent an immediate conclusion.

Como’s recruitment drive has included a strong focus on adding quality at centre-back, with the club looking to provide Cesc Fabregas with a proven option in defence. Chalobah has emerged as the leading target, and this latest round of discussions suggests the Serie A side are serious about seeing the move through.

From Chelsea’s perspective, the stance is understandable. Chalobah is coming off a productive campaign in which he made 34 Premier League appearances and scored three goals, while also featuring eight times in the Champions League. Those numbers reflect both availability and trust, two attributes that naturally strengthen his market value.

There is also context around the player’s standing. Chalobah’s form over the past season helped earn England recognition under Thomas Tuchel for the World Cup, even if his involvement at the tournament was limited to a brief appearance in the third-place play-off against France. His profile has risen, and Chelsea are negotiating accordingly.

The expectation now is that Saturday’s meeting will be important. Whether that leads to a breakthrough may depend less on the headline fee and more on how the bonuses are shaped. As things stand, this is a live negotiation, active, serious and still open.

As a Chelsea supporter, this feels like one of those situations where the club simply has to stay disciplined. Chalobah has had a very good season, and if Como want him after that level of output, then Chelsea are right to hold firm on the valuation. A guaranteed £30m for a player with Premier League and Champions League experience is hardly unreasonable in the current market.

There is also a lot to like about how the club appear to be handling it. If Como want a lower fixed fee and more bonuses, Chelsea should only agree if those add-ons are realistic and likely to be triggered. There is no need to rush this one. Chalobah has shown he can contribute at a high level, and that gives Chelsea leverage.

From a fan point of view, there is always a bit of hesitation when an academy-connected player is involved, because supporters naturally want those stories to succeed at Stamford Bridge. But football decisions have to make sense strategically and financially. If Chalobah is not central to the long-term plan, then selling at the right price is smart business.

Overall, this report sounds encouraging for Chelsea. The interest is genuine, the numbers are respectable, and the club appear calm rather than pressured. That is usually a good sign when negotiations reach this stage.

title: Piers Morgan calls LeBron James the ‘Cristiano Ronaldo of basketball’ following 76ers move
description: LeBron James gets compared to Cristiano Ronaldo after joining the Philadelphia 76ers. LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo are undoubtedly freaks of nature as they continue to play their respective sports, despite being 41 years old.
fullText:
LeBron James gets compared to Cristiano Ronaldo after joining the Philadelphia 76ers.

LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo are undoubtedly freaks of nature as they continue to play their respective sports, despite being 41 years old.

While Ronaldo has joined a less competitive league, the same cannot be said for James, as he recently joined one of the best teams in the NBA, the Philadelphia 76ers.

Popular journalist and Ronaldo superfan Piers Morgan recently reacted to the news of James joining Philly. Morgan shared a message of support for King on Instagram.

“Amazing move by LeBron James to leave the LA Lakers after eight years for the Philadelphia 76ers. He’s 41, has nothing left to prove, but is taking a massive pay cut to try and win one more Championship with a different team on a different coast.

“I’ve loved watching him at the Lakers but so admire this spirit and decision,” Morgan said.

Morgan wasn’t done as he then compared James to Ronaldo and wished him good luck for the next chapter of his NBA career.

“He’s the Cristiano Ronaldo of basketball. Good luck, LeBron, and thanks for all the wonderful times at the Lakers. PS: You won’t be wearing shorts playing golf in Philly in the winter,” Morgan concluded.

title: Fenerbahce submit bid for Aston Villa target Rafael Leao
description: Aston Villa are facing a serious battle in the race to sign AC Milan winger Rafael Leao.According to Italian newspaper Gazzetta, Turkish giants Fenerbahce have leapfrogged Villa and are now considered...
fullText:
Aston Villa are facing a serious battle in the race to sign AC Milan winger Rafael Leao.

According to Italian newspaper Gazzetta, Turkish giants Fenerbahce have leapfrogged Villa and are now considered frontrunners to sign Leao after tabling a significant bid.

Villa are on the market for a winger to replace Morgan Rogers, who recently completed a British record £117 million move to Chelsea, and Leao is one of several names under consideration.

The Portuguese international is expected to leave Milan this summer, but Villa aren’t the only club keeping tabs on his situation.

Their reluctance to act on their interest could now come back to bite them, with Fenerbahce seriously pushing to beat Villa to the signing of the Portuguese winger.

Rather than considering an initial loan deal, the Turkish giants are looking to strike a permanent deal.

They are reportedly willing to offer Milan an initial €40m (£34m) for the 27-year-old, with performance-related bonuses potentially taking the total value of the transfer to €50m (£43m).

Fenerbahce are simultaneously hoping to reach an agreement with Leao on personal terms. They have reportedly offered him a five-year contract worth a guaranteed €8m (£7m) per season.

On top of that, he could earn an additional €1.5m (£1.2m) if he makes more than 20 appearances in a season, another €1.5m if he scores at least 15 goals, and a further €1m (£854k) if Fenerbahce win the Turkish Super Lig.

Leao still has two years left on his contract with Milan but has been heavily linked with a move away from San Siro Stadium for months.

He’s coming off an underwhelming campaign where he managed 10 goals and three assists in 31 games across all competitions, which is poor by his high standards.

However, there’s no doubt that Leao can be a game-changer when he performs at a high level.

Villa will have to beat Fenerbahce’s proposal to lure Leao to Birmingham, although he has repeatedly been linked with a move to the Premier League.

At the moment, Unai Emery’s side are focusing on other targets, including Chelsea duo Alejandro Garnacho and Nicolas Jackson.

title: The new Manchester City manager is determined to help City’s golden boy shine
description: Earlier this week, Manchester City announced that Phil Foden had extended his contract with the club until the summer of 2030. It is clear that City are backing Foden to return to his dazzling best af...
fullText:
Earlier this week, Manchester City announced that Phil Foden had extended his contract with the club until the summer of 2030. It is clear that City are backing Foden to return to his dazzling best after two tough and trying seasons for him. New City manager Enzo Maresca is aiming to help Foden on that path and if he succeeds, it will help shape Manchester City into a formidable unit.

When Enzo Maresca faced the media yesterday for the first time as Manchester City manager yesterday, he said that he aiming to help Phil Foden return to his best form. The Italian manager added that it is his duty to do so. Speaking on Phil Foden, Maresca said: “I just want to help Phil to be the Phil we all want. First of all for him because he needs to enjoy football and second because I know how good he is. Phil in a good shape and mood, he can win games.”

“Treble season he was fantastic, season after he won Player of the Year. He struggled a little bit, but I told him it’s my duty to help him. He’s from the house. He’s from me. He’s a City fan.“

A big variable over the 2026-27 season for Manchester City is which Phil Foden they will get. Will the 2023-24 Player of the Season Foden return? The hope is that after a summer of rest this is what occurs. Or will Foden continue to be the inconsistent player he has been over the past two seasons? Foden is too good a player to not be a key player for the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. Hopefully the saying that class is permanent and form is temporary rings true for Foden this season.

Enzo Maresca is determined to help Phil Foden find his best once again. Maresca has worked with Foden previously, and that does give Maresca a template to use to guide Foden. He knows what makes Foden tick, and that should aid Maresca in his quest to help the England international. It seems that is what Maresca is determined to do as he explained yesterday.

Enzo Maresca is aiming to help Phil Foden become a vital component of Manchester City’s side. If he can succeed in his goal, it will be huge for the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders as Foden is a bonafide match-winner that City will need firing throughout next season and beyond.

title: Sam Kerr scores first goal after Gotham return, Emily Sonnett taken off field on stretcher
description: Seven years after she left the National Women’s Soccer League as its most prolific scorer, Sam Kerr marked her return to the league with her first goal since rejoining Gotham FC, an equalizer against Portland Thorns. The Australia striker was her own toughest critic, admitting she did not think much of her overall performance at Providence Park. fullText:
Seven years after she left the National Women’s Soccer League as its most prolific scorer, Sam Kerr marked her return to the league with her first goal since rejoining Gotham FC, an equalizer against Portland Thorns.

The Australia striker was her own toughest critic, admitting she did not think much of her overall performance at Providence Park. But her goal in the 62nd minute saw Gotham tie 2-2, adding to goals from Midge Purce, Renee Lyles and Jessie Fleming. Jayden Perry was later sent off for the Thorns.

“I’m obviously happy to score, help the team, but I expect more from myself,” Kerr said post-match. “So I wasn’t too happy with how I played. Quite disappointing, to be honest.

“I thought we were quite poor today. But we’re probably lucky to get away with the tie in the end. I guess I am happy… that we didn’t lose.”

Kerr’s return has been one of the most significant acquisitions in Gotham’s history. The 32-year-old signed with the reigning NWSL champions through the 2030 season after leaving Chelsea this summer, returning to the club where she starred when it was still known as Sky Blue FC.

Emily Sonnett’s return to Providence Park, meanwhile, lasted just 11 minutes as the Gotham defender was taken off on a stretcher after appearing to suffer a left knee injury.

In the seventh minute, Sonnett sprinted to challenge Thorns forward Pietra Tordin for the ball and seemed to make little contact before collapsing to the turf. She immediately grabbed her left knee and signaled toward the Gotham bench for medical assistance.

After several minutes of treatment on the field, Sonnett was placed on a stretcher and carried off to a standing ovation from the Portland crowd, which remembered the former Thorns defender fondly. Mandy Freeman entered the match in her place.

Gotham said Sonnett will undergo further evaluation after the team returns to New Jersey and she won’t play Gotham’s next match against Bay FC in San Jose. The club expects to share more information on the player’s injury early next week.

The 32- year-old has rarely missed time through injury during her professional career but the implications of any absence would be significant for Gotham and the U.S. women’s national team, with the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil less than a year away. Emma Hayes has consistently relied on Sonnett’s versatility, deploying her wherever the squad’s greatest need arose, whether at center back, fullback or defensive midfield.

title: Barcelona will not change their transfer plans even after key midfielder’s long-term injury
description: Frenkie de Jong’s injury update earlier this week confirmed that the player would miss a big part of the opening of the new season, as he has ruptured the medial collateral ligament of his knee.The ...
fullText:
Frenkie de Jong’s injury update earlier this week confirmed that the player would miss a big part of the opening of the new season, as he has ruptured the medial collateral ligament of his knee.

The development comes as a massive blow to Hansi Flick’s plans, for De Jong has proven to be instrumental as a starter alongside Pedri in recent years for the club.

Having the club captain out to yet another injury blow, needless to say, leaves the club in a relatively tricky situation with only Pedri, Gavi and Marc Bernal left as the options to play in the deep midfield.

Further, it makes the operation of Marc Casado’s departure complicated too.

As reported by Mundo Deportivo now, Barcelona have no intention of changing their transfer plans after De Jong’s injury and will rely only on internal solutions until he is back.

Flick will not change his transfer plans. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

Hansi Flick considers that he has enough players in midfield to fill the void, both in the current first-team squad and in the academy, and will rely on them to run the midfield.

After all, it is not a new situation for Flick to find himself in as he already played out the final stretch of last season without De Jong and with the same midfield options at his disposal.

The club managed to defend their lead in La Liga quite comfortably at that time, and he believes there is no reason they cannot tide them across the crisis once more.

At the crucial final stretch of last season when the Dutchman was out, it was between Marc Bernal and Gavi who joined Pedri at the base of midfield as part of the double pivot.

Bernal could see more prominence in the coming season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Both players are coming off long-term injuries, but they both ended last season on highs and will be better rested and fresh to begin the new season even as starters. Clearly, they will be the two options that appeal to Flick the most.

Further, the manager has the likes of Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen as options to play as defensive midfielders if need be, while Xavi Espart also offers a strong solution to the problem.

In the academy, Brian Farinas and Tommy Marques are two strong candidates who stand out and will be evaluated in pre-season. Dani Olmo and Fermin Lopez, in the worst scenario, can also drop down and join the double pivot.

According to talkSPORT, Leeds are already in ‘advanced talks’ with City and the 23-year-old is leaning towards a move to Elland Road.

Leeds have been searching for a new first-choice keeper since Karl Darlow joined Manchester United.

Lucas Perri was Leeds’ first-choice keeper last season, but his performances were far from convincing, forcing the club to explore other options.

Leeds can also turn to Alex Cairns, but they’ve now set their sights on Trafford, making him the leading candidate to take over between the posts.

Trafford is keen to leave City after struggling for regular first-team football, and Leeds are ready to extend an olive branch.

However, despite being described as an ‘incredible’ goalkeeper by former City manager Pep Guardiola, Trafford was forced to play second fiddle to Gianluigi Donnarumma, who joined on deadline day.

The Italian became Guardiola’s first-choice option, leaving Trafford to spend most of the 2025/26 season on the bench despite his impressive reputation.

The Englishman made 17 appearances across all competitions last season, featuring in every EFL Cup and FA Cup match as City lifted both trophies.

Trafford has made it clear that he wants to play regularly, even if that means leaving City again.

During the 2024/25 Championship campaign, Trafford was one of the division’s standout players, helping Burnley secure promotion while conceding just 16 goals in 46 league matches.

Leeds know exactly what Trafford can offer and are ready to make him their highest paid player.

They battled Burnley throughout that promotion race and saw first-hand how difficult he was to beat.

His performances also earned him a spot in the England team before making his international debut in March. He was also part of Thomas Tuchel’s squad at the World Cup.

title: China’s memory chip makers ride AI boom to new power — and U.S. scrutiny
description: SINGAPORE, July 24 () - For months, Chinese chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had been hiking prices on Huawei, one of the country’s biggest technology companies. The chipmaker held firm when Huawei demanded relief from the escalating costs, according to two people familiar with the matter.
fullText:
SINGAPORE, July 24 (Reuters) - For months, Chinese chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had been hiking prices on Huawei, one of the country's biggest technology companies. The chipmaker held firm when Huawei demanded relief from the escalating costs, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The standoff came to a head on CXMT's factory floor in June. A group of engineers from a chipmaking-equipment vendor with deep strategic ties to Huawei had been working in the cleanrooms at CXMT's core research and development zone in Hefei, Anhui province. Without warning, CXMT ordered the engineers, who had been helping with equipment maintenance, to pack their tools and ‌leave the factory floor immediately, the two sources said.

Executives at the Huawei-connected equipment vendor, SiCarrier, concluded the confrontation was the result of the power struggle between CXMT and Huawei, the people told Reuters. The companies still do business but the engineers haven't been allowed back into the R&D zone, the two people said.

CXMT, Huawei and SiCarrier didn't ‌respond to questions about the incident.

The clash illustrates the changing dynamics of China's semiconductor industry. CXMT has risen to become the world's fourth-biggest maker of memory, including the DRAM variety used in smartphones, laptops and servers. Now, the company is powerful enough to charge prices even Huawei can't stomach.

Memory chips that help devices run apps and store files were once a low-margin business. CXMT and its flash-memory counterpart, Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp, or YMTC, spent years relying on ​government funding and racking up losses.

But the global buildout of AI data centers has transformed the humble components into one of the world's most sought-after products, sparking battles over pricing and a scramble for supply. The Chinese memory makers are now picking clients and dictating prices, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters. In some cases, they are charging more than their larger South Korean rivals, Samsung and SK Hynix, as skyrocketing demand for memory chips forces Chinese buyers to pay ever-higher prices.

CXMT this month signed a five-year agreement with ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese owner, worth more than $7 billion, three people familiar with the arrangement told Reuters. ByteDance didn't respond to a request for comment about the deal, which hasn't been reported previously.

This account of how CXMT and YMTC are wielding their newfound clout is based on interviews with more than a dozen people, including executives, engineers, suppliers and U.S. officials, and a Reuters review of 50 Chinese government policy documents and company disclosures. It reveals new details on their pricing power, strategies and dealmaking as both companies – known in China as the "twin stars" of memory – race toward blockbuster IPOs.

title: All you need to know about the 2026 off-road Gran Fondo
description: Details of the routes, timings and road closures for the weekend are revealed.
fullText:
The Gran Fondo Isle of Man returns this weekend with a new off-road format, marking the biggest change in the event's 10-year history.

Taking place on Saturday and Sunday, the cycling festival has moved away from its traditional road route in favour of a multi-surface challenge featuring gravel tracks, green lanes, forest trails and historical railway lines.

Organisers said the redesigned course had been created to reflect the Island's landscape and the growing popularity of gravel cycling, while remaining true to the event's focus on endurance and participation.

The flagship Gran Fondo Gravel and Gran Fondo XC MTB races take place on Sunday, with riders setting off from Ramsey at 09:30 BST before finishing about 60 miles (100km) later in Port Erin.

The point-to-point route takes competitors to the island's northern tip before heading south through farmland, wetlands, moorland, forests and coastal scenery.

It features 30 designated off-road and C-road sectors, including Ballacorey Farm, The Curraghs, The Kella, Ballacarnane Farm, Archallagan Plantation and Eary Cushlin, before a final climb over Bradda Head and a technical descent into Port Erin.

Organisers described it as "a route shaped by the island itself", rather than adapting an existing road course.

The event begins on Saturday with two warm-up events.

The 'Minisculo Fondo' starts at 11:00 on a fully closed half-mile circuit around Mooragh Park in Ramsey, offering children and families the chance to take part.

It is followed at 13:00 by the Gran Fondo Challenge, a non-competitive 30-mile (50km) event that starts and finishes in Ramsey and is designed for riders looking for a shorter off-road experience or a warm-up ahead of Sunday's races.

The name Gran Fondo has its origin in Italian cycling, and points to endurance challenges and long distance.

The Isle of Man Gran Fondo is a qualifying competition for the UCI Gran Fondo World Series.

The UCI Gran Fondo World Series said it adopted the "Gran Fondo" name to connect with a continental mass-participation cycling tradition.

The Isle of Man Gran Fondo has organised large-scale cycling events on the Island for more than a decade, beginning with the Isle of Man Cyclefest in 2016 before launching the Gran Fondo series.

The event has previously attracted riders ranging from first-time cyclists to professional racers, including Sir Mark Cavendish, Ben Swift, Lizzie Holden and Anna Christian.

After hosting road-based events for 10 years, organisers said the move to gravel and mountain bike racing reflected "the sport's changing landscape" while "showcasing more of the Island's natural environment".

Several temporary road closures will be in place during the Gran Fondo weekend to allow the event to take place safely.

On Saturday (between 10:00-12:00), closures will affect:

North Shore Road — from its junction with Park Road to its junction with Ballacloan Road

On Sunday (between 09:00-12:00), closures will take place across several areas as riders make their way from Ramsey to Port Erin.

Ballacorey Road — from its junction with Bride Road to the entrance of Ballacorey Farm

Smeale Road — from its junction with Bride Coast Road to the entrance of Public Right of Way U79

Leodest Road — from the entrance of Public Right of Way 25 to its junction with Bride Coast Road

Bride Coast Road — from its junction with Kiondroghad Road to its junction with Polly Road

Polly Road — from its junction with Bride Coast Road to Public Right of Way 9

Old Windmill Road — from its junction with Ballamona Road to its junction with Old Sulby Road

Old Sulby Road — to its junction with Clenagh Road

Kella Road — from its junction with Clenagh Road to its junction with Kella Close

On Sunday (between 10:00-15:00), closures will be in place on:

Brack A Broom Lane — from its junction with the A20 Poortown Road to its junction with Glen Mooar Loop Road

Sloc Road — from its junction with D60 Lhagg Road to its junction with Public Right of Way 197 / Surby Mill Road

On Sunday (between 10:00 - 18:00), closures will affect:

Station Road — from its junction with Falcon Hill U129 to its junction with Shore Road
