title: NBA Trade Rumors: After LeBron James Decision, Massive Moves Ahead
description: NBA trade rumors are back in swing now that the league has gotten LeBron James' decision. He is heading to Philadelphia ... and now what? The post NBA Trade Rumors: After LeBron James Decision, Massive Moves Ahead appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Well that’s that. LeBron James has shocked the NBA and made a remarkable choice, opting to play for the Sixers for the next two years in a move that will have massive reverberations around the league. And we’re now ready to kick the old NBA trade rumor mill back into gear.

So what is coming next? We asked, let’s look …

James Harden. There was some question as to whether the Cavaliers would work as a unit if both Harden and James were on the team alongside Donovan Mitchell. Now, that won’t be an issue. But the Cavaliers now will have to finish up their summer with a contract for Harden and some sort of way to fill out the roster–they can add at least one more player, and they’ve been linked to DeMar DeRozan, Mario Hezonja and Jonathan Kuminga. Of note: The Cavs do want to give significant minutes to young players Meleek Thomas and Jaylon Tyson this season.

Draymond Green. The Warriors were holding off on signing Green in hopes of adding James. Now that James is off the board, the Warriors will give Green their remaining cap room but will still be on the lookout for another addition–they’re in the market for DeRozan and Hezonja. There’s an outside chance that the Warriors could move Moses Moody in a deal, and may have interest in Cam Johnson.

Peyton Watson. The Nuggets are still holding out hope to keep Watson in restricted free agency. Now that the James situation is settled, the Nuggets could finally seek to trade away Cam Johnson, who has not been the target that many expected thus far. The Nuggets have rebuffed interest in Johnson so far, but that could change.

Mario Hezonja. Hezonja has made his return to the NBA a notable one, as he has been one of the best players in the Spanish league after flaming out during three stops in the league after he’d been the No. 5 overall pick. Can Hezonja still play? That’s unclear but he’s done well to hype himself up as a contributor for contenders who are now bidding on his services.

Jonathan Kuminga. This has been the big donut in the coffee of the NBA offseason, and Kuminga remains the subject of sign-and-trade rumors. But the Hawks do not want players back, and will want some draft compensation no matter what. Can they get anyone to pay it? The Cavs are a longshot, as are the Lakers, and there are expected to be others in the mix.

DeMar DeRozan. He was waived by the Kings, and it is unlikely he will follow James to the Sixers. Miami? Cleveland? Warriors? His options are open.

Bradley Beal. The Miami Heat? That makes the most sense for Beal, who has been linked to the Celtics, Cavaliers, Warriors and others.

Bronny James. Will he join his father in Philadelphia? Many think he should stay in Los Angeles, including some with the Lakers who have liked his development. It should be time to sink or swim in the NBA for Bronny James, but if his dad wants him in Philly, that’s where he will go.

Well, no one expected Anthony Davis and Kyrie Irving to pop back up on the NBA market here in late July but, the rumor mill is never-ending. Neither is expected to get moved, but they’re still being talked about  …

Anthony Davis, Wizards. (Remaining contract: two years, $121 million, including player option.) Davis has been the subject of much speculation this offseason, but around the league, there isn’t a sense he is going to be dealt. The Wizards would like to get Davis on the floor and see if he can help them compete for a playoff spot. If not, he could be dealt by the February trade deadline.

Zion Williamson, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: two years, $87 million.) We’re not expecting Williamson to be moved by the end of the summer, but if he stays on the floor early in the year, New Orleans has plenty of incentive to find a new spot for him. A frontcourt of Derik Queen and Williamson makes little sense.

Kevin Durant, Rockets. (Remaining contract: two years, $90 million, player option.) There does not seem to be a market for Durant, who is 37 and has $90 million over two years on his contract. Rumors of Pistons interest has faded as the focus there is on re-signing Jalen Duren. Maybe a Durant deal comes back up after that gets done? It’s a longshot.

Jamal Murray, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: three years, $160 million.) The Nuggets are on track to operate over the second apron, which is not a place any team–especially a Kroenke team–likes to operate. Dealing Murray could shave some money off the cap but he was an All-Star last year and dumping him might be too much to ask of the Nuggets.

Jimmy Butler, Warriors. (Remaining contract: one year, $57 million.) It just does not appear that the Warriors are looking to move Butler. He’s the team’s main path to adding another star, as he is probably out until Christmas or later as he recovers from January ACL surgery. There are not many teams looking to add a rehabbing 36-year-old to their mix, and the Warriors are not likely to find a player who is better than Butler when healthy.

It’s hard to bring in a young star–or even a young potential star–on the trade market. But there could be some wrangling for these guys, the 25-and-under (OK, 26 for Trey Murphy) crowd.

Moses Moody, Warriors. (Remaining contract: two years, $26 million.) Moody him self said he is “curious” about what will happen to him on the trade market. Will James’ decision change that? He has developed into a valuable piece for Golden State, but a nasty knee injury could keep him out for most of next season.

Jalen Duren, Pistons. (Remaining contract: restricted free agent.) Sign-and-trade options for Duren are all but extinguished–were the Pistons ever really weighing a deal with the Kings for Domantas Sabonis? The Pistons have made moves to be able to give Duren more money, and that’s the likely way this all plays out.

Trey Murphy, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: three years, $88 million.) Murphy is a favorite in NBA trade rumors, but there are questions on how serious New Orleans would be about trading him. One exec says it will take a Desmond Bane-style offer (four first-round picks) to pry him from New Orleans, though that price has dropped a bit. Still, there’s been no movement yet.

Peyton Watson, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: restricted free agent.) The long restricted free-agent slog is on for Watson, and the Nuggets have surprised many by not being aggressive in moving players to create some breathing room to keep Watson. The sign-and-trade market reportedly includes the Clippers, Hawks and Bucks, but there is not much yet that would attract the Nuggets’ attention on a deal.

Nikola Jovic, Heat. (Remaining contract: four years, $62 million.) There is trepidation about trading for Jovic, who is certainly available and is still only 23 years old. But the remaining contract is a hefty bite for teams to take.

LeBron James will create an NBA trade rumor ripple effect, and the East could feel it most.

Michael Porter Jr., Nets. (Remaining contract: one year, $40 million, partial guarantee.) Porter is in the final year of his deal and wants an extension that starts at about what he is making now. The Nets likely won’t go that high, and if no middle ground is found, we are in for another heap of trade talk. Even if Porter is extended, he could be a trade candidate by next February’s deadline.

Grant Williams, Hornets. (Remaining contract: one year, $15 million.) The Hornets are not quite done with their roster, and Williams’ expiring deal has some value. He can still be a worthy big man off the bench.

Royce O’Neale, Hornets. (Remaining contract: two years, $21 million,) The Hornets would not be able to trade O’Neale with anyone else yet, so they could wait on a deal. But the team has gotten calls about moving him on after he’s come over from the Suns.

Jarrett Allen, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: three years, $90 million.) As with Mobley, if the Cavs entice LeBron James to Cleveland, Allen could be trade bait. It’s more likely that Allen gets traded than Mobley, and the Cavaliers could get some relief and a contributor. Allen is a standard offensive center but is a valued rim-runner who can protect the paint.

Max Strus, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: one year, $16 million.) The Cavs are trying hard to fit everything under the second apron, and that likely means moving off Strus, if they can find a taker.

Dennis Schroder, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: one year, $14.6 million.) Schroder has played for 11 teams in the NBA so far, and the Cavs would be open to making it 12 as they seek to duck the second apron and still stay in the contending picture.

Myles Turner, Bucks. (Remaining contract: three years, $80 million.) Two things may well both be true on Turner–the Bucks are not shopping him because they want some veterans on hand, and there is no interest in him from other teams because of his contract.

Kyle Kuzma, Bucks. (Remaining contract: one year, $20 million,) His expiring contract is attractive and if the Bucks pull a sign-and-trade for Peyton Watson, Bennedict Mathurin or Jonathan Kuminga, he figures to be involved.

Jake LaRavia, Lakers. (Remaining contract: one year, $6 million.) Hustles, plays every game, but inconsistent. His contract makes him an attractive piece, though.

Herb Jones, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: four years, $82 million, including player option.) Jones is a popular name on the market, but the Pelicans are said to want two first-round picks, and with Jones having struggled with injuries and his 3-point shot in the past two seasons, that’s probably too steep. His remaining contract scares off potential suitors, too.

Derrick Jones Jr., Clippers. (Remaining contract: one year, $10 million.) Jones is a defensive ace still, and his expiring contract gives the Clippers some wiggle room to move him. They’re caught in the Aspiration pause, however.

Rudy Gobert, Timberwolves. (Remaining contract: two years, $74 million, including player option.) The Wolves, according to a report in The Athletic, were offered Jaylen Brown with the Celtics wanting Rudy Gobert, plus picks, as part of a trade package. The Wolves turned that down, though there still has been interest in Gobert, who is up for an extension.

Keldon Johnson, Spurs. (Remaining contract: one year, $17.5 million.) The reigning Sixth Man of the Year is heading into the final season of his contract, and San Antonio is likely to phase out his minutes in favor of younger players. He is still a valued leader on the team, but he could be a chip worth cashing in if the Spurs can land a first-round pick.

Domantas Sabonis, Kings. (Remaining contract: two years, $93 million.) Sabonis has had some nibbles, but no bites. There was a rumor that the Hornets were planning to trade for him, but that proved fruitless. Then there was the Jalen Duren sign-and-trade with the Pistons, which was far-fetched from the beginning. This one might have to wait until the season gets going.

Jrue Holiday, Blazers. (Remaining contract: two years, $72 million, with player option.) Certainly, something has to give in Portland with the arrival of Morant. Holiday is not getting any younger, but he has value around the NBA.

Zach LaVine, Kings. (Remaining contract: one year, $49 million.) LaVine picked up the player option worth $49 million. There was some hope that he could be waived, but after the Kings let DeMar DeRozan go, they’ll keep LaVine on the books and hope they can find a place to dump him.

Aaron Gordon, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: three years, $110 million.) Gordon has struggled to stay healthy, but is still a valued connective piece when he plays. He needs to be a No. 3/4 option on a good team, and teams aren’t falling over themselves to cough up assets for that, and the Nuggets have not pushed hard for a trade.

Daniel Gafford, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: 3 years, $54 million.) Gafford will be 28 in October, and with the Mavs focused on getting younger, moving him along has been one of the team’s top options. The concern is whether the guy the Mavs want to be their stalwart center–Dereck Lively II–can stay healthy. Lively has played 98 games in three seasons.

PJ Washington, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: 4 years, $90 million.) Like Gafford, Washington is aging out of the Mavericks’ timeline, as he turns 28 this summer. He’s a stretch 4 who plays good defense, but his shooting has been suspect–he made just 32.5% of his 3s last year. Washington’s extension kicks in this year, though, so he might be a better trade target down the line.

Klay Thompson, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: one year, $17 million.) Another aging Mav! Thompson does not fit Dallas’s timeline, and if the Mavs can get anything–youth, a few second-rounders–for him, they will. He’s still a 38% 3-point shooter. The addition of Tarik Biberovic is more incentive to move Thompson.

Cam Johnson, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: one year, $23 million.) Johnson has been a disaster in Denver, and he has been a prominent feature on the NBA trade rumor mill for years now. He still has enough of a reputation around the league to warrant trade interest, but a report from The Stein Line suggests the Nuggets are not going that route … yet.

The NBA trade rumor mill has had a busy summer, interspersed with some controversy. Here are the top rumors that sprouted into actual trades …

Boston’s controversial decision to move Brown as he neared an extension on a supermax contract set off a round of second apron discussion in the NBA.

Celtics get: Paul George, a 2028 first-round pick that could convert to a swap, Philly’s 2031 unprotected first-rounder, and two second-round picks.

The deal that kicked off the summer was the one most expected to be expanded, but wound up staying a two-teamer. The Bucks are banking on this being enough for a rebuild, and the Heat were hoping this precedes a LeBron James return. Alas …

Bucks get: Tyler Herro, Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakucionis go to Milwaukee. Also Bucks got the 13th pick in the draft (Nate Ament) and future first-rounders, in 2031 and 2033, plus a future pick swap and a second-round pick.

Heat get: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis.

The Wolves combined their two major transactions, taking a chance on bringing in LaMelo Ball and getting off the contract of Julius Randle.

Timberwolves get: LaMelo Ball, Josh Green, No. 33 pick (Isaiah Evans).

Hornets get: Naz Reid, Mouhamadou Gueye, rights to Matteo Spagnolo, Minnesota’s first-round pick in 2033, second round picks in 2029, 2032 and 2033, plus three swaps, also from Minnesota.

Nets get: Julius Randle, No. 28 pick (Joshua Jefferson).

Memphis finally moves on from Ja Morant, and was able to do so by taking on Jerami Grant’s contract–but did not have to include outgoing draft capital.

Grizzlies get: Jerami Grant and Kris Murray.

A classic NBA deal that started as Isaiah Stewart going to Memphis, but ballooned since.

Grizzlies get: Isaiah Stewart, D’Angelo Russell, AJ Johnson, five second-round picks. (Lose: Santi Aldama.)

Pistons get: John Collins, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris. (Lose: Isaiah Stewart, Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser.)

Clippers get: Trade exception. (Lose: John Collins.)

Wizards get: Khris Middleton. (Lose: D’Angelo Russell.)

Bucks get: Caris LeVert. (Lose: Taurean Prince, Gary Harris, AJ Johnson.)

Mavericks get: Santi Aldama, Marcus Sasser. (Lose: Khris Middleton.)

Now,  this trade has been undone punishment for the Aspiration scandal has yet to be doled out, but it’s still likely to get done once that situation is settled. There are still a lot of questions about when that might be, though.

Clippers get: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks (2031 and 2033), plus a swap and two second-round picks.

The Hornets had been looking for a taker for Bridges, whose past domestic violence charges scared off many teams. But Charlotte attached draft capital and the Suns took him in.

Suns get: Miles Bridges, 2029 first-round pick, 2027 second-round pick.

Hornets get: Grayson Allen, Royce O’Neale, 2033 first-round pick.

The Thunder jettisoned Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins for second-round picks early in July, and got all the way under the second apron by moving Lu Dort later in a three-team deal that saw former No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher dealt, too.

Hawks get: Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard.

Thunder get: Three second-round picks.

Mavericks get: Zaccharie Risacher.

title: Reports: Juve still in contact with Parma for Zion Suzuki; Benfica’s Anatoliy Trubin added to list of goalkeeper options
description: When is the time to pivot to another option besides Emi Martinez? That day could be fast approaching.
fullText:
As he talked with the Italian press following Juventus’ first friendly of the summer this past Saturday, head coach Luciano Spalletti confirmed what we all pretty much knew by now: “It’s true that we’re looking for a goalkeeper to be even more competitive.” It was a question about the situation regarding the status of the starter in goal from the previous two seasons, Michele Di Gregorio, and how the summer transfer activity (or maybe lack of it) is going to play into plans for the upcoming season.

We’ve known for quite a while that Aston Villa keeper Emi Martinez is Juventus’ clear-cut choice to replace Di Gregorio. However, that is going about as well as Juve’s attempt to sign Alisson Becker from Liverpool late in the spring — yeah, that’s why the Bianconeri pivoted to Martinez in the first place.

So, as the days go by and no movement on the Martinez front continues to be the norm, the day in which Juventus pivot again looks more and more likely. But who will that pivot be toward?

We know that Guglielmo Vicario of Tottenham has been the main name thrown out there as a backup option if the pursuit of Martinez ultimately ends up like Juventus’ attempt to sign Alisson. (You know, something that doesn’t happen despite all the rumors.) According to Sky Italia, Juventus CEO Giovanni Carnevali continues to be in contact with Parma regarding a potential deal for Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki if things with Martinez don’t work out like it’s starting to trend toward.

There’s also been another name thrown out there besides Vicario and Suzuki: Benfica goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin, who Juventus reportedly have interest in, according to Italian transfer reporter Nicolo Schira. Trubin was also included in a report about potential Martinez alternatives by English journalist Ben Jacobs last weekend.

#Juventus have asked info for #Benfica’s goalkeeper Anatoliy #Trubin and #Parma’s gk Zion #Suzuki. Dibu #Martinez (Aston Villa) is #Juve’s main target, but there is no agreement between the clubs, as of now. #transfers

— Nicolò Schira (@NicoSchira) July 23, 2026

So, yeah. Just like a lot of the other parts of Juventus’ current summer mercato, the process of getting a new starting goalkeeper in place of Di Gregorio has been anything but fast and swift. You can blame the change in front office leadership. You can blame former CEO Damien Comolli for his inability to close on signing Alisson before the Frenchman was ousted for Carnevali. You can blame a whole lot of things.

The bottom line is that Juventus still don’t have somebody to replace Di Gregorio, who is once again going to be in goal for Juventus second friendly of the summer on Saturday night against Standard Liège in Belgium.

We know that Suzuki would be expensive, with previous reports saying his price tag would be in the neighborhood of €30 million. It’s unclear how much Trubin would actually cost, but one has to think considering his age (25 years old in a week) and the club in which he currently plays for (Benfica), then a €30 million price tag feels like the bare minimum.

So yeah, if Juventus are hesitant to pay Aston Villa what they want for Martinez, it might be tough to get a goalkeeper like Suzuki or Trubin for something that’s considered an affordable transfer fee. Vicario is probably the most affordable option of the three previously mentioned, but there is a reason for that — and it’s pretty easy to figure out that Tottenham want to sell him this summer after he was not called up for their preseason tour in Australia.

title: Former Sharks Forward Finally Finds a Home for the 2026-27 Season
description: After multiple months of speculation and reports out of Russia linking him to a return to the Kontinental Hockey League, it appears former San Jose Sharks forward Kevin Labanc will be departing the KHL after just a single season.
fullText:
After multiple months of speculation and reports out of Russia linking him to a return to the Kontinental Hockey League, it appears former San Jose Sharks forward Kevin Labanc will be departing the KHL after just a single season.

After leaving North America to play for the Shanghai Dragons during the 2025-26 campaign, Labanc was able to rejuvenate his career overseas. He scored 15 goals and 34 points in 55 games for the Dragons, earning a spot in the KHL All-Star Game in the process.

There was belief at one point that Labanc would sign with Salavat Yulaev Ufa early in the offseason, then it was reported by Russian media that he was nearing a deal with Ak Bars Kazan, but neither move came to fruition. Now, Labanc has officially signed a one-year deal with the SC Rapperswil-Jona Lakers in the Swiss National League.

During his time in teal, Labanc played 478 games. He scored 82 goals and 225 points as a member of the San Jose Sharks before joining the Columbus Blue Jackets for a single season.

title: Angels Must Keep Building Prospect Pool At Trade Deadline
description: The Los Angeles Angels have a lot of talent that they can offload at the trade deadline and need to continue improving the farm system.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels have a lot of eyes on them as we approach the Aug. 3 trade deadline as the team has several players that are of interest for contending teams.

The Angels have several players that fit a massive position of need for many teams around the league: controllable starting pitchers and right-handed bats.

Left-hander Reid Detmers and right-hander José Soriano have been great this season and are under contract through 2028, making them attractive adds for any team seeking pitching help (which is just about every buying team).

The price to acquire either pitcher is going to be steep because of how intense bidding wars can get between executives that want the same player, and Angels owner Arte Moreno should be aware of that.

The same goes for shortstop Zach Neto, who is under contract for several more years and is one of the top power-hitting middle infielders in the game. Neto leads the league in strikeouts but also leads the league in runs scored and is coming off back-to-back 5-plus WAR seasons at 25-years-old.

Moreno needs to let interim general manager John Mozeliak take charge and move controllable assets for massive hauls to continue growing the farm system that doesn’t have a ton of high-level prospects.

Los Angeles’ prospect pool had just one top 100 prospect (right-hander Tyler Bremner, MLB No. 43) coming into the season and despite a strong draft from the scouting team this year, the farm system still needs a lot of improvement.

ESPN's Kiley McDaniel thinks the Angels farm system is starting to get healthier and praised their recent draft returns.

“Improving and with a better long-term view, given the most recent first-round pick, RF/LHP Jared Grindlinger, means the first-round draft approach is similar to what it is in the later rounds,” McDaniel wrote Friday.

“The returns on prep picks in the past few drafts -- LHP Johnny Slawinski, RHP Dylan Jordan, RHP Trey Gregory-Alford, LHP Talon Haley and RHP C.J. Gray, among others -- have been positive, and that points to a likely improvement in scouting and development behind the scenes.”

Slawinski (Angels No. 4), Jordan (No. 7), Gregory-Alford (No. 8), Haley (No. 11) and Gray (No. 12) have pitched pretty well in the minors this season and could end up somewhere on next year’s top 100 list, but the Angels could add prospects that are firmly on the list already if they moved at least one of Detmers or Soriano and Neto among others like outfielder Jo Adell or designated hitter Jorge Soler.

McDaniel believes the Angels need star talent, which is counterintuitive to selling your best players, but they need to reset and acquire a bunch of young talent.

“Continuing to lean into players they think they have an edge in developing should be the focus.”

This is an extremely important deadline for the Angels – their players may never have as much value as they do right now.

title: Damian Rzepecki vs. Magomed Zaynukov prediction, pick for UFC Fight Night 282
description: The lone lightweight bout on the main card is between Damian Rzepecki and Magomed Zaynukov. Will "Chanco" win his debut?
fullText:
Damian Rzepecki and Magomed Zaynukov meet on the UFC Fight Night 282 main card Saturday at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Check out this quick breakdown of the matchup from MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom.

Rzepecki (10-0 MMA, 0-0 UFC) makes his UFC debut. In 10 fights, the undefeated Polish fighter has only seen the judges' scorecards one time, scoring finishes with strikes and submissions on the regional scene.

Zaynukov (8-0 MMA, 0-0 UFC) debuts after an appearance on Dana White's Contender Series. Also undefeated, Zaynukov has five wins by KO/TKO stoppage and three decisions.

Filling out the main card is a lightweight fight between Damian Rzepecki and Magomed Zaynukov.

Despite having a solid fight on the Contender Series, Zaynukov has arguably become more popular among fight fans after being memed as the infamous "John Pork." However, despite the memes and his affiliations with dominant grapplers like Islam Makhachev, Zaynukov carries a solid muay Thai arsenal that can't be overlooked.

Still, Zaynukov's opponent, Rzepecki, is also not someone to underestimate.

A well-rounded MMA native, Rzepecki is a southpaw-primary stance-switcher who offers offense in multiple phases. That said, the Polish newcomer has been out-muscled in the clinch and wrestling phases before, and may be a notch down in the athleticism department in comparison to his counterpart.

For that reason, I'll officially pick Zaynukov to edge out a decision win in a fight that I suspect will play out much closer than the current odds indicate.

The oddsmakers and the public favor the Russian fighter, listing Zaynukov -300 and Rzepecki +235 via FanDuel.

Rzepecki and Zaynukov are expected to walk to the cage at approximately 1:10 p.m. ET. The fight streams live on Paramount+.

title: Tracking Corey Seager’s progress toward return to Texas Rangers
description: Texas Rangers star shortstop Corey Seager took live batting practice Friday, the latest step in his return to the active roster. ARLINGTON — All reports this week, from manager Skip...
fullText:
Texas Rangers star shortstop Corey Seager took live batting practice Friday, the latest step in his return to the active roster.

ARLINGTON — All reports this week, from manager Skip Schumaker to the man himself, indicated that Corey Seager is moving closer to returning to the Texas Rangers after a second absence caused by a bad back.

The shortstop on Friday attempted to simulate, as best he and the Rangers could, a rehab game at Globe Life Field. He took at-bats, then sat between them. He fielded groundballs and ran the bases, too.

The goal is for Seager to do that again Saturday or Sunday, depending on when the Rangers can find a reliable arm from Double A Frisco or Triple A Round Rock to come to Globe Life Field to pitch to the two-time World Series MVP.

A rehab assignment is being discussed. If left to Seager, he will go straight to the Rangers’ lineup once the medical staff gives him the green light. It might be left to Seager, though Schumaker won’t object if he wants to go somewhere for a few games.

The situation is fluid, it’s safe to say, but one thing that seems consistent is no one is willing to commit to a game when Seager will return. Maybe that’s the nature of back injuries, or maybe it’s the nature of Seager’s knack for being injured.

Maybe he’ll be back Monday for the finale in a critical series against the Mariners, which started Friday night. Maybe he’ll end up meeting the Rangers next Friday in Houston for another critical series against the Astros.

At least they’re talking about a return, and at the right time as the Rangers navigate the most important stretch of their season so far.

“I don’t feel strongly about him having an extended rehab. If he wanted a game or two, then I’m OK with that, too,” Schumaker said. “He just hasn’t played games in a while, but I would tell you the setup that we have going is almost like a rehab assignment. But it’s just tough to mimic certain things.”

Seager seems to have conquered the movements that made his back balk most — running and bending at the waist. That’s good, because a batter needs to run and a shortstop needs to bend at the waist.

The Rangers need Seager as they make their push for the playoffs, but, more urgently, their push to convince club brass to make additions at the Aug. 3 trade deadline. The Rangers entered Friday in first place in the American League West, albeit with a .500 record (51-51) and by only a half-game over the Mariners.

Friday’s game was the first of 10 remaining until the trade deadline, and a rough four games against the Mariners in this weekend wrap-around series might make the front office reconsider an investment in player acquisitions.

They might be completely sold with a good series.

While Seager appears close to returning, third baseman Josh Jung might need the injured list after a test of his left calf didn’t go well Friday. Schumaker said that Jung couldn’t get to full speed when running and might have been lucky to get to 50 percent.

Catcher Danny Jansen said that he’s not headed toward elbow surgery, at least not yet. He’s throwing at 90 feet with some oomph and will give things two more weeks before deciding if he can trudge through the rest of the season.

That’s curious timing, considering the Rangers just lost catcher Kyle Higashioka to a similar injury. That is now a need position for the Rangers at the deadline, though they might roll the dice if Jansen can manage the injury.

The Rangers also need bullpen help, though the healthy returns of starting pitchers Jack Leiter, Jordan Montgomery and Cody Bradford could produce multiple multi-inning relievers by mid-August. Montgomery, who was scheduled to make his final rehab start Friday night for Triple A Round Rock, could become a rotation option next week.

Leiter said that he plans to throw off a mound Saturday. If all goes well with his left ankle, he could begin what he hopes is a short buildup back to the rotation.

But the main injury news, as it is every time he is injured, is Seager. If he comes back, and if it’s soon, he could influence the Rangers’ decision-making ahead of the trade deadline.

Jeff Wilson, jwilson@alldlls.com

title: Astros' Spencer Arrighetti leaves start against White Sox in second inning
description: Houston Astros right-hander Spencer Arrighetti left his start against the Chicago White Sox in the second inning Friday night with an apparent injury.  Arrighetti was throwing warmup pitches before starting the second inning when he was visited at the mound by manager Joe Espada, pitching coach Joshua Miller and a trainer.
fullText:
CHICAGO (AP) — Houston Astros right-hander Spencer Arrighetti left his start against the Chicago White Sox in the second inning Friday night with an apparent injury.

Arrighetti was throwing warmup pitches before starting the second inning when he was visited at the mound by manager Joe Espada, pitching coach Joshua Miller and a trainer. After a short discussion, Arrighetti left the game and was replaced by AJ Blubaugh.

There was no immediate word on the reason Arrighetti left the game with the Astros trailing 3-0.

Arrighetti struggled in the first inning, allowing three runs and two hits with two walks and two hit batters while throwing 33 pitches. He entered the game 7-5 and has a 4.60 ERA and hasn't won since May 28, when he was 7-1.

title: Cincinnati Bengals: Depth improved at cornerback
description: Jul. 24—The Cincinnati Bengals found a combination of cornerbacks that worked last year with Dax Hill and DJ Turner II solidifying themselves as the top two on the outside and Jalen Davis stepping in as an effective nickel. However, they also worked to improve the room with a couple of key additions this offseason, and whether that just improves the depth or impacts what the starting lineup ...
fullText:
Jul. 24—The Cincinnati Bengals found a combination of cornerbacks that worked last year with Dax Hill and DJ Turner II solidifying themselves as the top two on the outside and Jalen Davis stepping in as an effective nickel.

However, they also worked to improve the room with a couple of key additions this offseason, and whether that just improves the depth or impacts what the starting lineup looks like is still to be determined.

The Bengals used a third-round pick on Tacario Davis, who brings elite length and could be a succession plan for either Hill or Turner.

The two veterans are in contract years, and it seems unlikely the organization could keep both. Hill or Tacario Davis could be candidates to move inside if defensive coordinator Al Golden wants a way to get all three players on the field.

It could take some time for Tacario Davis to acclimate, though, and there's no rush. Ja'Sir Taylor signed in free agency to compete with Davis, so Cincinnati has some options inside.

Outside corners DJ Ivey and Josh Newton could be competing for a roster spot as well.

Let's take a look at the past performances of the Bengals' current cornerbacks, and how they are expected to stack up in 2026 with help from some analysis and data from Pro Football Focus.

This is the last in a series of pieces breaking down each position group for the Bengals before training camp begins July 29.

Cornerbacks on the rosterProjected starters: Dax Hill, DJ Turner II, Jalen Davis

Reserves: Tacario Davis, DJ Ivey, Ja'Sir Taylor

Others in the mix: Josh Newton, Bralyn Lux, Jalen Kimber, Ceyair Wright

Hill by the numbers2025 stats: 88 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 10 missed tackles, 11 passes defended, 1 interception in 17 games, all starts.

PFF grades for 2025: Hill ranked 49th of 114 cornerbacks in defense grade (64.9), 36th in coverage grade (67.7), 77th in pass rush grade (50.4) and 54th in run defense grade (60.0).

Turner by the numbers2025 stats: 40 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 5 missed tackles, 2 interceptions, 18 passes defended, 1 fumble recovery in 17 games (16 starts)

PFF grades for 2025: Turner ranked 19th of 114 cornerbacks in defense grade (73.3), sixth in coverage grade (78.1) and 105th in run defense grade (37.9).

Jalen Davis by the numbers2025 stats: 77 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 1 interception, 1 pass defended, 1.0 sacks, 1 forced fumble in seven games, three starts

PFF grades for 2025: Jalen Davis did not play enough snaps to qualify for a rankings but posted a defense grade of 65.5, pass rush grade of 85.4, coverage grade of 65.1 and run defense grade of 57.1.

Further analysisNo Bengals cornerbacks were among the top 20 when PFF.com put together its final rankings at the end of the 2025 season, though Turner might have been in the mix based on his overall defense and coverage grades.

Turner was the team's most consistent cornerback, though he got a slow start with a poor training camp. He's now taking on a bigger leadership role in the Bengals' secondary and a near lock for the No. 1 cornerback spot. Turner received votes in ESPN's top 10 cornerbacks poll of NFL executives, coaches and scouts, but did not make the list.

Hill came back from a 2024 ACL tear to impress and settled into a clear role last season after starting his NFL career as a free safety, then moving to slot corner and finally to the outside before his knee injury. He wants to stay put in that spot, but Tacario Davis' arrival once against brought Hill's role into question.

Jalen Davis was thrown into action late last season and proved himself capable in the nickel role, but he hasn't shown it over the course of a full season yet. He'll need a standout preseason to maintain that spot. Ja'Sir Taylor has been a spot starter throughout his four NFL seasons, including just one start last year in an eight-game stint with the New York Jets. He saw a maximum of six starts in 2023 with the L.A. Chargers, but he also could challenge for the job in Cincinnati.

If Tacario Davis makes the adjustment quickly and pans out as a rookie, the Bengals' depth at cornerback should be much better in 2026.

title: Juan Soto leaves Mets' game vs Dodgers with calf soreness
description: Amid ongoing concerns about a calf injury, Juan Soto exited the Mets' game against the Dodgers with soreness.
fullText:
NEW YORK — The same issue that has relegated Juan Soto to a designated hitter role ended his night prematurely on Friday night.

Soto was removed from the Mets' contest with the Dodgers before an at-bat in the bottom of the sixth inning with left calf soreness, the club announced.

Since the second half began, Soto has spent four of his six games in the DH position. He sat in Wednesday's series finale with the Brewers to receive an extra day of rest after he partook in the All-Star Game festivities one week prior in Philadelphia.

Soto drew two walks before he departed Friday's game and was replaced by Jorge Polanco with the Mets and Dodgers locked in a 1-1 tie. He also left the club's series opener out of the break against the Phillies on July 16 with the same malady.

The Mets now have a full complement of outfielders back since Luis Robert Jr. returned earlier in the week from a three-month stint on the injured list with a herniated disc in his back.

This season, Soto is slashing .283/.408/.539 with 21 home runs, 52 RBI and 46 runs. He missed roughly two weeks in early April with a low-grade calf strain in his right calf.

Check back for more updates on Juan Soto's status following Friday's early exit.

title: Jacoby Brissett isn't participating in 11-on-11 drills
description: Yes, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is practicing as he tries to get a contract that pays him like a starter, not a backup.
fullText:
Yes, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is practicing as he tries to get a contract that pays him like a starter, not a backup. But he's not really practicing.

As noted by Darren Urban of the team's official website, Brissett "isn’t participating in 11-on-11 drills yet."

That's surely a direct result of his dissatisfaction with a deal he signed under the impression that he wouldn't be the team's QB1. Now that he's the presumptive Week 1 starter, he's seeking an adjustment.

The current range for veteran starters begins in the low $20 millions and stretches into the $60 millions. With Brissett currently at $6.5 million per year, triple that to $19.5 million and call it a day.

He'd be the lowest-paid veteran starter, while still making much more than he's due to make.

And it would help get him as ready as he can be with a new coaching staff and a new offense. Which is even more critical, given that the Cardinals are in a division with three Super Bowl contenders.

Who would have thought that the Cardinals would long for the days that they were the which-doesn't-belong-and-why fifth team in the NFC East?

A Barbie is in the house 💕

Barbie is officially in the house, and Reese once again knows exactly how to make an entrance.

title: Assumption takes down Wahlert Catholic for Iowa baseball state title
description: Davenport Assumption won its 12th Iowa high school baseball championship with a win over Wahlert Catholic on Friday.
fullText:
Davenport Assumption, as the No. 7 seed in the Iowa high school state baseball tournament, won its program's 12th championship on Friday, July 24, with a 5-3 win over Wahlert Catholic.

The Knights became the first-ever No. 7 seed in any classification to win the state title, and the first program in Iowa history to win 12 baseball titles.

“You can’t really explain it, it's awesome,” said senior Nolan Dittmer. “We worked at this for four years, and we didn’t start off great this season, but now we are finished. We came into this tournament knowing that we’re not really a seven seed.”

Cooper Sweeney helped make that history, leading the way on the mound in the victory over the Golden Eagles.

Sweeney was a shutdown pitcher in the quarterfinal win over Carlisle, going 5 ⅔ innings, allowing just one run. On Friday, he did the same, pitching five innings with seven strikeouts and five hits allowed on 82 pitches.​

Because he only pitched 63 pitches on Tuesday, Sweeney was required two days of rest and was in line to start in the biggest game of his young freshman career. Sweeney held the Golden Eagles to just two hits going into the fourth inning.

More: Iowa high school state baseball tournament 2026: Scores, brackets

“He’s tough as nails,” said Assumption coach Greg Thissen. “He might be a freshman, but he didn’t look like it today. He looked like a season vet today.” ​

A Dittmer single in the third scored the Knights' first run of the game, and in the next at-bat, Jack DiIulio also singled, driving in two runs to make it 3-0.

Dittmer would have another RBI after a double brought in Sam Hughes. In the top of the sixth, Eli Egger doubled to score DiIulio, to make it a 5-0 Assumption lead.​

Wahlert had a real scoring threat in the bottom of the sixth, with two singles from JP Elbert and Noah Krapfl, leading Sweeney’s day ending after five+ innings of work.

Bailey Alvarez, who had 34 innings of work as a pitcher this season, came in and got the first out of the inning, but then a single from Graham Ahler and two walks made the score 5-2 with one out.

“That’s one thing you're going to get from us every time is a fight,” Elbert said. “This group of guys just has that fight in them. We had that comeback walk-off against North Polk and we fought to the end, love them to death.”

More: Des Moines Register seeks fall high school sports intern

Colton Mosher replaced Alvarez after 19 pitches and got the final two outs of the frame, but not before the third walk of the inning that scored to make Wahlert's deficit just two runs, 5-3.

Mosher ended the game in the seventh, leading the Knights to yet another state crown, their first since 2018.

“Our seniors, I can’t talk about them enough,” Thissen said. “They were all big today and they all contributed today and in this programs turnaround.

This article originally appeared on Des Moines Register: Assumption takes down Wahlert Catholic for Iowa baseball state title

title: Anthony Joshua Vs. Kristian Prenga Start Time, Ring Walks And Weigh-In Results
description: Anthony Joshua weighed 251 pounds and Kristian Prenga 261.4 ahead of Saturday's main event. Here are the start time, ring-walk timing, weigh-in results and full card.
fullText:
Anthony Joshua is back in the boxing ring on Saturday in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Joshua will take on Kristian Prenga in the headlining fight of another strong Saudi boxing card. While Joshua is expected to handle Prenga, there is some pressure. The battle with Tyson Fury — who just stopped Mariusz Wach on Friday — is reportedly signed, sealed and ready to deliver. Joshua needs to come away from his fight with Prenga victorious. Here’s everything you need to know about the card. Let's talk boxing.

Event: Anthony Joshua vs. Kristian Prenga, "The Comeback"

Date/venue: Saturday, July 25, 2026 · Jeddah Superdome, Saudi Arabia

Main card start: 1 p.m. ET / 10 a.m. PT / 6 p.m. BST

Main-event ring walks: approximately 5:45 p.m. ET / 10:45 p.m. BST

Weigh-in: Joshua 251 lbs · Prenga 261.4 lbs

Broadcast: DAZN pay-per-view, $59.99 US / £19.99 UK (included with DAZN Ultimate)

Records: Joshua 29-4 (26 KOs) · Prenga 20-1 (20 KOs)

The main card is set for 1 p.m. ET / 10 a.m. PT / 6 p.m. BST, with main-event ring walks penciled for roughly 5:45 p.m. ET, though that slides with how the undercard runs. The show streams on DAZN pay-per-view from the Jeddah Superdome at $59.99 in the U.S. and £19.99 in the U.K., with the card also folded into the DAZN Ultimate tier.

It also shares the date with the Errol Spence Jr. vs. Tim Tszyu card in Sydney, so Saturday runs wall-to-wall from Jeddah in the afternoon to Australia in the small hours.

At Friday's official weigh-in on the Jeddah waterfront, Joshua tipped the scale at 251 pounds and Prenga came in at 261.4, leaving the Albanian about 10 pounds heavier for the night. It was Joshua's heaviest in years — up 7.6 pounds from the 243.4 he carried against Jake Paul in December, and just shy of his career-high 255.4.

The extra mass reads as a deliberate play for power against a naturally bigger, come-forward opponent.

Beneath the main event, the 13-bout card carries two title fights: Hamzah Sheeraz defends his WBO super-middleweight belt against Simon Zachenhuber, and Josh Kelly defends the IBF junior-middleweight title against Caoimhin Agyarko. Reito Tsutsumi, Oleksandr Khyzhniak and India's Nishant Dev round out the notable names.

It is a deep Riyadh Season-style bill built to keep the crowd invested well before the headliner.

What will an impressive performance from Joshua look like? The margin for error as it pertains to winning and losing may not be small, but it is if we're talking about winning in the court of public perception. Anything short of a stoppage will draw criticism. Even if Joshua stops Prenga and takes some visible damage or is rocked, people will question if he is fit to face Fury.

Joshua trained alongside Oleksandr Usyk's team for this camp and has spoken about being pushed to "show greatness," a nod to the scrutiny that comes with Fury already working the microphone at his expense.

title: Dayton Dragons: Acosta, pitching, clean play lead to 4th straight win
description: You could call all the breaks the Dayton Dragons got Thursday, July 23, lucky. But manager Julio Morillo wouldn’t. For starters, Cedar Rapids committed six errors. The Kernels didn’t stop there, contributing in many other ways to the Dragons’ cause. So much that only three hits didn’t prevent the Dragons from winning 5-3 at Day Air Ballpark to extend their winning streak to four games.
fullText:
You could call all the breaks the Dayton Dragons got Thursday, July 23, lucky. But manager Julio Morillo wouldn’t.

For starters, Cedar Rapids committed six errors. The Kernels didn’t stop there, contributing in many other ways to the Dragons’ cause. So much that only three hits didn’t prevent the Dragons from winning 5-3 at Day Air Ballpark to extend their winning streak to four games.

“Lucky … you can put it that way, but we also created those things,” Morillo said. “That’s part of the game. You create those situations. And capitalizing on the mistakes that they make, that’s the game as well.”

Cedar Rapids entered the game with 110 errors in 90 games. Their six errors Thursday equaled a season high. The Kernels’ record is 37-54 and 6-21 in the second half. Paraphrasing a bit what former NFL coach Dennis Green famously said, the Dragons could say, “They are who we thought they were.”

The Kernels started by committing errors like a pro golfer who can’t stop making bogeys, four in the first three innings and five in the first five.

Add these mistakes to the mix in the first five innings while the Dragons (51-40, 12-13) took a 4-2 lead: three hit batters, three walks, a balk, a wild pitch (scored a run), two unearned runs, five stolen bases allowed and a Little League inside-the-park homer.

One Dragons hitter had a memorable night. Victor Acosta, batting ninth as the DH, scored three runs all by himself.

In the second inning, he tripled to the left-field corner. And when shortstop Jose Salas took the cutoff throw, turned and threw wildly to third, Acosta scored easily for a 2-0 lead.

In the fourth, Acosta hit his fourth homer for a 3-1 lead. The fan who caught the home run on the left-field lawn with his bare hands made the best defensive play of the night against the Dragons.

In the eighth, Acosta walked, stole second and third, and scored on a throwing error by catcher Enrique Jimenez, as he stole third, for a 5-3 lead.

“It’s exciting because we come in here every day to practice and then just go into the game to make it happen,” Acosta said. “Everything is fun, we make the playoffs, and we’re just excited to be here every day.”

The Dragons are relying more on stolen bases than they did while winning the first-half East Division title. They don’t have as much home run power as they did with Alfredo Duno, Carter Graham and Kien Vu. Morillo said the plan for this series is to take advantage of the Kernels’ inability to control the running game.

Acosta, Tyson Lewis, Peyton Stovall and Marcus Smith each stole two bases. The eight stolen bases tied the club record achieved two other times.

The Kernels’ trouble began in the first inning when Ryan McCrystal reached on an infield error with one out. Then, Julio Carerras was hit by a pitch, and Lewis reached on another error to load the bases. With two outs, Jacob Friend was hit by a pitch for a 1-0 lead.

The Dragons made the score 4-2 in the fifth. Lewis reached base when the first baseman dropped a throw. He stole second and moved to third on a balk. When Mason Neville struck out for the second out, Lewis scored on a strike-three wild pitch.

The errors, the baserunning, all of it, were needed. The Dragons were 0-for-13 with runners in scoring position and left nine runners on base. Other than Acosta’s two big hits, only Smith had a two-out single in the seventh.

The Dragons committed no errors — neither did Roof Man with a late-game appearance — and three pitchers held the Kernels to four hits. They manufactured two runs against starter Luke Hayden and homered against Trent Hodgdon in the eighth.

Hayden made his fourth start since being on the injured list with a hamstring strain from late April to July 4. He’s an important part of the rotation the Dragons will need to pitch well in the playoffs.

Hayden pitched 4 ⅔ innings, equaling his longest start this month, and allowed two runs on three hits and two walks. He struck out six, including three in order in the fourth.

“I feel back to normal,” Hayden said. “I feel like my leg is healthy. Just continuing to go out there and pitch more and work through a couple things and get a little stamina back. That’s one area where I could improve on. But other than that, I feel good.”

The two at-bats he wants back are a walk and a hit batter to No. 9 hitter Andy Lugo. He scored the first time and moved a runner ahead who scored the second time. When his pitch count hit 82 in the fifth, Morillo pulled him.

“I would like him to win more counts, but that takes time,” Morillo said. “His stuff is really good, but we just need to get him to win the counts so he can go deeper in the games.”

Hayden was backed by Victor Diaz (2-0) who allowed nothing in 2 innings and struck out five, including the side in order in the seventh. Hodgdon pitched the final two innings, struck out four and earned his sixth save.

“Victor and Trent, they’re dudes and their stuff speaks for themselves,” Hayden said. “That’s the whole motto is just attack guys relentlessly and get hitters on their heels. And I think that’s exactly what we did tonight.”

Plus, control the running game, play error free and watch Acosta run around the bases.

title: Patrick Mahomes turned rehab into a competition. No surprise he's winning | Opinion
description: Patrick Mahomes' torrid comeback from a serious knee injury is both a physical and mental feat, columnist Jarrett Bell writes.
fullText:
ST. JOSEPH, MO – It would have been fitting enough if the Kansas City Chiefs had rolled out a red carpet at Scanlon Hall on Friday and lined the path with trumpets blaring as Patrick Mahomes arrived.

Sure, it’s only the start of training camp at Missouri Western State University – and rookie camp at that – but this is a big deal nonetheless.

Mahomes is here! And so is his left knee, surgically repaired, rehab-fortified and lathered up. The best quarterback in the NFL hit another milestone in his comeback journey, cleared to fully practice in any and all drills from Day 1 of camp.

“I’m excited,” Mahomes confirmed during a 12-minute news conference inside the players' dorm. “I’ve been seeing cinder block walls rehabbing every single day in Kansas City.”

When Mahomes checked in, it had been 223 days since he was carted off the field at Arrowhead Stadium with a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

Shoot, back in the day an injury like that might have wiped out a player for a year-and-a-half. Yet here was Mahomes, 30, tracking to make it back for the Monday night regular season opener against the Denver Broncos on Sept. 14.

Here’s to modern medicine and advanced rehab. Mahomes got the clearance on Wednesday during a follow-up exam with his surgeon, Dan Cooper.

“This is just another checkpoint on the schedule, you know?” Mahomes said, offering obligatory caution to go with some extreme confidence. “And so, you have to continue to work. It’s not over and I’m not going to play a game tomorrow. You’ve got to continue to work and get better and better and go through all practice, and prove to the coaches, prove to the doctors and everybody that I’m the same quarterback I was before, if not better.”

It was telling that Chiefs coach Andy Reid won’t even rule out playing Mahomes in the preseason. That decision is for another day, and Reid is quick to maintain that they are still operating on a day-by-day assessment. When someone asked about the Week 1 target that Mahomes has always had in sight, Reid said, “You’ve got to see how things go there. Let’s just see where we’re at and not make any predictions or anything else.”

Still, Reid, whose team stumbled to 6-11 last season as the Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, knows how his quarterback is wired better than any of us. And I’d suspect that even if he doesn’t want to risk a setback during the preseason, there’s no need to declare anything definitive now. If I’m Reid, I’m pushing whatever buttons will keep the flow of this mojo moving.

Mahomes knows. This is not about being ready to rock for the preseason.

“We’ll just see when we get there,” he said. “Like, I’m a competitor, so, like game day, I’m gonna want to be out there. But I understand the process of getting myself ready in the regular season is more important, but we will see. I mean, the coaches and doctors will kind of make that decision for me, but I’ll prepare myself like I’m going to play. And then if I’m doing a ‘very hard warmup,’ I will take that as serious as playing in the preseason game.”

Listen to Mahomes and it is so apparent that recovering physically from such a serious injury constitutes just one significant portion of a comeback. It’s mental, too.

He reached out to Tom Brady for advice. It’s a striking coincidence that Mahomes, whose resume includes three Super Bowl rings, suffered his severe knee injury in his ninth season. Brady had won three Super Bowls, too, when he suffered a similar injury. It’s probably a given that Mahomes has connected with his former teammate, Tyreek Hill, over the course of his rehab. Hill, currently a free agent, is rehabbing from a dislocated kneecap and torn ACL and LCL.

Then there’s Zach Ertz, the free agent tight end who suffered a torn ACL a week before Mahomes was injured, while playing with the Commanders. Mahomes and Ertz (who was once coached by Mahomes’ college coach, Kliff Kingsbury) have struck quite a supportive bond with each other during their respective rehabs.

“We kind of had like competitions on where we were at and where we were rehabbing,” Mahomes said.

After they compared notes on how much they could deadlift in the weight room, Mahomes said, the “competition” advanced to include video exchanges. Ertz sent Mahomes a video showing his explosion in drills jumping on a box; Mahomes sent Ertz footage that captured him cutting to change direction.

“And so, it keeps the competition going,” Mahomes said. “It’s a long process and you feel like sometimes you’re lonely because you’re just doing stuff by yourself and you’re just competing against yourself. So, it gave me someone else that I can compete with to kind of push my competitive drive.”

Mahomes, given his abundance of competitive juice, mentioned “how much it hurt me” to watch the Chiefs’ final three games last season without him. Yet that wasn’t the hardest element of his setback to deal with mentally.

“Honestly, the toughest part was at the beginning, like, not being able to get up and chase my kids around,” Mahomes, father of three, said, reflecting on the holiday season that came shortly after his Dec. 15 surgery. “Like, I know it sounds crazy, but being a dad and being an active dad, I always want to be around my kids and playing and stuff like that. And so, I think that was tough. Once I was able to do that, it kind of motivated me to kind of keep getting better. So, when Bronze (Patrick III) plays a T-ball game or Sterling’s playing soccer, I can be out there with them.

“I always knew that I was going to get back here. And it’s just because of my mindset and the people that we have around me.”

More mental challenges – or at least markers – loom. As much as Mahomes has something to prove with his performance – he aims to get the ball out of his hand quicker and expects to run less after posting a career-high 422 rushing yards last season – at some point he will take a hit on the knee.

Of course, as was the case during offseason workouts, that won’t happen during training camp as the quarterbacks, clad in yellow jerseys, are off-limits.

“We’ve had people kind of on air coming at me and you’re moving, but it’s not the same as having Chris Jones chasing after you, you know?” said Mahomes, who will start off wearing a brace on the knee but hasn’t been told whether he will need to wear it for an extended period.

Whenever he takes a hit, it’ll be another marker.

“You’ll never know until you get out there and you get hit and you make plays,” he said. “But I trust the process I’ve been through.”

Until last season, the most time Mahomes missed during his NFL career came in 2019, when he missed two games due to a dislocated knee. Like now, he returned at an accelerated pace – which undoubtedly says something about how he’s physically wired to recover at a pace that is not typical.

He reflected wistfully of a marker upon his return in 2019 that indicated he was fully back. It came on a play when he improvised while trying to avoid a rush to throw a pass. And it clearly provided some perspective to draw on in the coming weeks.

“I have that throw where I jump and throw the ball and it looks cool, but I actually did it because I was running my knee out of there,” he recalled. “So, it’s just little things like that, you just have to build that confidence back.

“I’m glad you could do that from Day 1 of training camp. You know, I didn’t want to have to get only a couple weeks of practicing and then have to go play in a game. I wanted to build it up.”

In other words, get ready to roll out the red carpet and strike up the band.

Follow Jarrett Bell on X: @JarrettBell

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Patrick Mahomes turned rehab into a competition. No surprise he's winning | Opinion

title: Exeter, Rochester open state legion baseball tournament with wins
description: Both the Exeter Post 32 and Rochester Post 7 American Legion baseball teams opened state tournament play with wins.
fullText:
NASHUA – Both Exeter Post 32 and Rochester Post 7 opened the annual American Legion State Tournament with victories Friday at Holman Stadium.

Exeter, the District B No. 2 seed, defeated District A No. 3 seed Laconia Post 7, 10-4, while District B No. 3 seed Rochester topped District A No. 2 seed Lebanon, 7-1.

"Always want to get the first win in the tournament," Exeter head coach Tim Mitropoulos said. "The team played hard. Wasn’t our cleanest game in the field or on the base paths, but the team played hard every inning and always responded when Laconia got a run or had a good inning offensively."

Rochester is making its first state tournament appearance since 2019.

"I told the boys they have to believe in themselves, and hopefully this win helps us," Rochester head coach Tim Locke said.

Exeter will face District A No. 1 seed Bedford at 4 p.m. on July 25, while Rochester will take on Nashua at 7 p.m. Bedford rolled past Salem, 18-4, while Nashua defeated Keene, 7-4.

"Going to be a great test," Mitropoulos said of facing undefeated Bedford. "We're excited about the opportunity."

Locke announced James Mabey will get the start for Rochester against Nashua.

"Nashua is a very good team," Locke said. "They finished in first for a reason, and they're an older team. But (Mabey) is a really good pitcher. If he comes out and sets the tone, I think it's going to be a good ball game."

Andrew Martin, Brady McGovern and Nate Gallant, the top three hitters in Exeter's lineup, combined to go 6-for-10 with six RBIs.

"Those guys have been consistent all year and give us a great chance every at-bat," Mitropoulos said. "They hit the ball hard and had a great day at the plate today. Our lineup was good today, and when guys got on at the bottom of the order, that gave those guys a great chance to keep our momentum going."

Martin went 3-for-4 with two RBIs and two runs scored, McGovern finished 2-for-3 with two RBIs and a run scored, and Gallant went 1-for-3 with two RBIs and a run scored.

Exeter took advantage of three Laconia errors that led to eight unearned runs.

"We want to try and put the ball in play and see what happens," Mitropoulos said. "Putting pressure on the defense that way is what we try to do. We did a good job of that today throughout the lineup."

Exeter's seven-run third inning broke open a close game and gave Post 32 a 9-4 lead. Exeter added a run in the fourth, while Laconia scored single runs in the fourth and fifth innings.

Cam Morrill added two hits and two RBIs for Exeter, while Jackie Prompradit had a hit and an RBI.

Rochester scored three runs in the fifth inning to take a 6-1 lead, then added an insurance run in the seventh.

A trio of Post 7 pitchers, led by starter Hunter Spencer and relievers Carter Hanson and Nate Cloos, held Lebanon to one run on five hits while striking out seven.

"Those three guys are always the stalwarts," Locke said. "(Spencer) set the tone for us, (Hanson) held it for us, and (Cloos) finished it off. All three guys were throwing strikes. It was pretty impressive."

Cloos, Alex Locke and Ty Lindsay each collected two hits for Rochester, while Felix Guerrero had a hit and two RBIs. Alex Locke, Brayden Comeau and Cooper Hanson each drove in a run.

"We're a young team, so when we have the pitching we had today and they're throwing strikes, I think we can compete with anyone," Locke said. "I'm happy for them, and I hope they're enjoying it."

This article originally appeared on Portsmouth Herald: Exeter, Rochester open state legion baseball tournament with wins

title: Mike McDaniel Could Be Under a Microscope This Season
description: Mike McDaniel has another opportunity to prove he’s one of the NFL’s brightest offensive minds. With Justin Herbert under center, success could put him back in the head coaching conversation while failure could reshape his reputation.
fullText:
When the Los Angeles Chargers hired Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator, they weren’t just adding another coach to the staff. They were bringing in one of the NFL’s most respected offensive minds, despite how his tenure as the Miami Dolphins’ head coach ultimately ended.

Now, the spotlight is on McDaniel in a way it hasn’t been in years.

His time in Miami was a tale of two stories. There were moments when his offense looked nearly unstoppable, built around speed, creativity and explosive play design. But as expectations grew, so did the criticism. The Dolphins struggled to consistently beat elite opponents and never made the deep playoff run many expected. Eventually, Miami decided it was time to move in a different direction.

That doesn’t erase McDaniel’s reputation as one of football’s brightest offensive innovators. If anything, it gives him an opportunity to remind everyone why he became a head coach in the first place.

This time, he has something he never had in Miami: Justin Herbert.

Few quarterbacks possess Herbert’s combination of arm talent, intelligence and toughness. While Tua Tagovailoa thrived in McDaniel’s system when healthy, Herbert offers a different dimension. He can attack every area of the field, make throws from impossible angles and create explosive plays even when protection breaks down.

That combination should make Chargers fans excited. It also raises the expectations.

The Chargers didn’t bring McDaniel in simply to maintain what they had. They hired him because they believe he can elevate an offense that has the pieces to become one of the league’s best. Herbert is entering another prime season. Omarion Hampton gives the offense a dynamic young running back, Ladd McConkey continues to develop into one of the NFL’s better young receivers and the offensive line has the talent to be among the league’s better units if it stays healthy.

If the offense takes a significant leap, McDaniel’s reputation will be restored almost overnight. Around the NFL, successful coordinators are always among the first names mentioned when head coaching vacancies open. Pairing an explosive offense with Herbert could quickly put McDaniel back on every owner’s shortlist.

On the other hand, if the Chargers’ offense stagnates or fails to maximize Herbert’s talent, the conversation changes. Fair or not, people will begin to wonder whether McDaniel’s previous success was more dependent on circumstances than his coaching. Questions that surfaced during the end of his Miami tenure will only become louder.

That’s why this season feels so important for him.

Coordinators rarely receive as much attention as head coaches, but McDaniel is an exception. His previous success, his innovative reputation and the opportunity to coach one of the league’s premier quarterbacks make this one of the NFL’s most fascinating storylines.

The Chargers have built a roster capable of competing for a championship. If McDaniel unlocks another level from Herbert and the offense, he’ll likely find himself back in the head coaching conversation sooner rather than later.

If not, this season may force the league to reevaluate just how much of an offensive genius he truly is.

title: Houston Texans Legend DeAndre Hopkins’ Next Career Move Is Completely Unexpected
description: The five-time Pro Bowler may swap his cleats for a clipboard, reuniting with Mike Vrabel in New England to mentor a new generation of NFL talent.
fullText:
After a decorated 13-year NFL career, former Houston Texans wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins could soon be beginning a new chapter on the sidelines instead of the field.

According to reports, Hopkins recently met with the New England Patriots to discuss a potential coaching role on Mike Vrabel's staff. The two are already very familiar with one another, having spent four seasons together in Houston from 2014 through 2017. Vrabel served as the Texans' linebackers coach and later defensive coordinator during that stretch, while Hopkins established himself as one of the league's premier wide receivers.

#Patriots HC Mike Vrabel says WR DeAndre Hopkins is with the team helping out in a potential coaching/personnel role as he figures out his future and what he wants to do next. pic.twitter.com/OY0t9N5gdp

— Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) July 24, 2026

Although the two worked on opposite sides of the ball, they were part of some of the Texans' most successful teams of that era. Hopkins developed into the focal point of Houston's offense, earning multiple Pro Bowl selections and first-team All-Pro honors while consistently producing despite frequent changes at quarterback. Vrabel quickly built a reputation as one of the NFL's brightest young coaches before eventually becoming the Tennessee Titans' head coach.

Their shared history makes the Patriots a logical landing spot if Hopkins decides coaching is the next step in his football journey. Vrabel has always emphasized relationships and accountability throughout his coaching career, and bringing in a respected former player who commanded the locker room during his playing days fits that philosophy.

Hopkins would also have plenty to offer New England's young receiving corps. Few receivers of his generation possessed his combination of elite hands, body control, route-running precision, and ability to win contested catches. Those traits helped him remain productive for well over a decade, and that knowledge could prove valuable for developing younger players trying to establish themselves in the league.

For Texans fans, the news serves as another reminder of Hopkins' lasting impact on the franchise. Drafted in the first round in 2013, he became one of the greatest receivers in team history, recording 632 receptions for 8,602 yards and 54 touchdowns during his seven seasons in Houston. Even years after his departure, Hopkins remains closely associated with some of the franchise's best teams and biggest moments.

Whether this meeting ultimately leads to an official coaching position remains to be seen, but it is an intriguing development for one of the most accomplished players in Texans history. If Hopkins decides his playing days are behind him, reuniting with Vrabel could be the perfect way to begin the next phase of his football career.

title: Azzi Fudd makes WNBA history with unprecedented 3-point contest victory
description: The Dallas rookie knocks down shot after shot in the Friday night event.
fullText:
Azzi Fudd makes WNBA history with unprecedented 3-point contest victory originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Azzi Fudd arrived at WNBA All-Star Weekend as the only rookie in the 3-point contest field. She left Chicago with the trophy and a place in league history.

The Dallas Wings guard won the 2026 WNBA 3-Point Contest on Friday night, becoming the first rookie ever to capture the event. Fudd delivered under pressure against a field of established long-range shooters, adding another major accomplishment to what has already been a memorable year.

“A historic night for Azzi Fudd,” the WNBA wrote on social media after her victory. “She’s the first rookie EVER to win the WNBA 3-PT shooting contest.”

Fudd defeated a six-player field that included Atlanta Dream star Rhyne Howard, Toronto Tempo guard Marina Mabrey, Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaun, Portland Fire forward Bridget Carleton and Seattle Storm guard Natisha Hiedeman.

The 23-year-old was the only first-year player invited to compete. She did much more than simply represent the rookie class.

Fudd has long been regarded as one of the smoothest shooters in women’s basketball. She showed exactly why on Friday. The Wings rookie remained composed while moving around the perimeter, knocking down enough shots to advance from the opening round and then finishing the job in the championship round.

A historic night for Azzi Fudd ⭐

She's the first rookie EVER to win the WNBA 3-PT shooting contest 👏 pic.twitter.com/gSYRLODZAr

— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) July 25, 2026

The contest included five traditional shooting locations, money balls worth two points and deep “From the Logo” attempts worth three points. That new wrinkle increased the difficulty, but it was not enough to stop Fudd from making history. Her victory was especially impressive considering the experience surrounding her. Mabrey and Howard had previously competed in the event, while every other player in the field had already established herself as a dangerous WNBA shooter.

Fudd was the newcomer. By the end of the night, she was the champion.

MORE: Angel Reese pops out in eye-catching Barbie look at WNBA All-Star events

The 3-point title is the latest chapter in Fudd’s rise from UConn star to one of the most important pieces of the Wings’ future. Dallas selected her with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft after a decorated college career. Fudd won a national championship with UConn in 2025 and was named the Final Four’s Most Outstanding Player after scoring 24 points in the championship game.

Her journey was not always smooth. Fudd battled multiple significant injuries during her career, including serious knee issues that cost her considerable playing time. She continued working through those setbacks and eventually developed into the player many expected her to become when she was the nation’s No. 1 high school recruit. Fudd entered All-Star Weekend averaging 13.2 points per game during her rookie season with Dallas. She has quickly become an important perimeter weapon for a Wings team also featuring Paige Bueckers and Arike Ogunbowale.

Now, Fudd owns a distinction no other rookie in WNBA history can claim.

Her first professional 3-point contest ended with a trophy, a record and one unforgettable night in Chicago.

title: When will 76ers and LeBron James have introductory press conference?
description: LeBron James announced his decision for the final chapter of his longstanding career. When will he be introduced in Philadelphia?
fullText:
LeBron James has announced his decision for the final chapter of his longstanding career.

James is expected to sign a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers and play alongside Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey in an effort to win the 76ers' first NBA championship since 1983, when the roster included Moses Malone, Julius Erving and Maurice Cheeks.

The 76ers swept Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Magic Johnson and the Los Angeles Lakers in four straight games that year.

Here's what we know about James' first potential press conference in Philadelphia:

More: 7 biggest winners and losers from LeBron James joining the 76ers

It remains unclear if LeBron James will have an official introductory press conference with the 76ers.

James did not have an introductory press conference with the Lakers when he joined the team in 2018. He did not speak to the media in Los Angeles until media day.

The four-time MVP has not participated in an introductory press conference since deciding to join Chris Bosh and Dwyane Wade as a member of the Miami Heat in 2010.

“There’s not going to be an introductory press conference,” said ESPN’s Brian Windhorst during the July 23 episode of “First Take.” “You don’t have to get it ready. After ‘not 5, not 6, not 7’ LeBron is done with introductory press conferences. … If he does one, it’ll be on his platforms and not an open thing that you’re gonna have.”

The social media conversation centered around James and the Miami Heat earlier this week about a potential return. Heat president Pat Riley and the Miami organization had been considered the odds-on favorites to land James after a blunder with the social media department.

Miami’s social media team accidentally published a scheduled YouTube livestream titled "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference." It was later deleted from the platform.
